title: fix(post): grblHAL, Carvera and TinyG write no motion after the no-plane refusal
body:
## What changed

`grblhal.cps`, `carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`: `xyFirst` now returns `false` when it refuses the first X/Y traverse because the stream states no ClearancePlane and no RetractPlane. Its callers write nothing for that move: `onRapid`, `onLinear`/`onCircular` (through `startXY`), and grblHAL's `onCycle`. X/Y stay unknown, so every later move of the section is refused the same way. The message is still given once per program. This is the rule the Tormach (#1614) and Fanuc-family (#1633) posts already follow.

Before this change, the refused rapid was still written as `G0 X20 Y10 Z2`, followed by the feeds. The app blocks the post on the warning, but the `post` CLI writes the file anyway, so the refused move ended up in the program text.

**TinyG too.** The issue says TinyG already stops through `startXY`. Its `onRapid` still wrote the combined rapid after the refusal, though, and the issue's "Done means" pin covers TinyG, so TinyG's `onRapid` gets the same guard. The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/1682-refused-traverse-writes-nothing.md`.

## Pinning tests (`crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance.rs`)

- `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name`: now also asserts that no motion line carries an X or Y word, for grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera. It was red on the old scripts (grblHAL output: `G0 X20 Y10 Z2`, `G1 X20 Y10 Z-1 F500`, ...).
- `no_xy_motion_follows_the_refusal_whatever_the_first_move` (new): the first move of the section is a feed, an arc or a canned cycle. For each case it checks that the refusal is given by name and that no X/Y word is written.

**Mutation check.** I reverted each new guard line on its own, ran the suite, restored the file from a backup, touched it and compared it with `cmp`. Every mutation turned the suite red:

| post | line mutated | result |
|---|---|---|
| grblhal / carvera / tinyg | `onRapid` guard dropped | 1 failed |
| grblhal / carvera / tinyg | `xyFirst` refusal returns `true` | 2 failed |
| grblhal / carvera / tinyg | `startXY` refusal check dropped | 2 failed |
| grblhal / carvera | `onLinear` guard dropped | 2 failed |
| grblhal / carvera | `onCircular` guard dropped | 1 failed |
| grblhal | `onCycle` guard dropped | 1 failed |

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. It ran 17 post suites (7 s) and 21 app suites, including `grblhal_post`, `carvera_post`, `tinyg_post` and `conformance` (97 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --test first_traverse_clearance -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No golden G-code changed. Only streams that state no plane are affected, and those were already refused.

## Not exercised

- The batch gate was not run, to keep within the budget.
- The Windows arms were not run.
- The app's posting path was not run end to end. It already blocks on the warning.

Changelog: grblHAL, Carvera and TinyG posts write no motion after refusing a first X/Y traverse with no stated clearance or retract plane (the `post` CLI no longer puts the refused move in the file)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1682

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe G76 J makes LinuxCNC's R1 ladder cut the record's passes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, `g76Grid`: J (first depth) is no longer floored to the grid on its own. LinuxCNC's G76 with `R1` cuts J, 2J, ... with the last pass clamped at K, so the control cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs (g76Why already holds the equal ladder), so J must satisfy (n-1)J < K <= nJ:

- J is the shallower grid rounding (as before) when that keeps the count;
- when the shallower J would add a pass, J is the one grid step up, and never a full grid step over the record's first cut;
- otherwise the record is refused by name: `G76 threading cycle refused - no first depth J on the control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes (K ...)`.

The root keeps its outward rounding. Peak, root, I and K are unchanged.

## Golden change, line by line

`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`, one line:

```
-G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
+G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0315 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
```

What this relies on, from the public LinuxCNC G-code reference (G76): J is the first cut depth, K the full thread depth (diameters here, under G7), and `R1.0` selects constant depth, so each pass goes J deeper than the last and the last pass is clamped at K.
- Old: 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942, then 0.0944 (a 0.0002 in pass) = 4 passes. The record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius).
- New: 0.0315, 0.0630, 0.0944 (clamped) = 3 passes, the record's count. J 0.0315 in is 0.000004 in (0.1 um) over the record's Ø0.8 mm first cut. The root (X + I - K) is the same as before: never deeper than the minor.
- P, Z, I, K, R, Q, H and every other line are unchanged. The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is byte-identical.

The earlier PathPilot Hub 8L sim run of this golden (PR #517 comments) does not cover the new J: **this golden needs a new Hub run** (not done here, no Hub access).

Scan (local script, not committed): realistic records (first depth 0.05-0.5 mm, height 0.3-2 mm, four minor diameters, the stream's lattice) - the old rule mis-stated 2.7% of inch records; the new rule miscounts none and refuses none in either unit. Refusals are reached only by records with many tiny rungs (e.g. 0.15 deep in rungs of 0.012, inch) or a lattice disagreement on the crest.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder.rs`:
- `g76_words_cut_exactly_the_records_passes_in_mm_and_inch` - parses the posted J/K as grid steps, counts ceil(K/J) and asserts it equals both the G33 pass count of the same document and ceil(height / first depth) of its record; asserts J is under one grid step over the record's first cut.
- `g76_refuses_by_name_when_no_grid_j_cuts_the_records_passes` - mm: crest +2 um (inside the lattice allowance) makes K 2.402, refused (J 0.801 would be a full step heavy); inch: 0.15 deep in 0.012 rungs, K 118 steps, no whole J with 12J < 118 <= 13J, refused.

Updated: `a_thread_posts_as_one_g76_block_with_the_option_in_mm_and_inch` (inch line J0.0315, golden regenerated).

Mutation checks (each mutation applied, suites run, file restored and touched):
- delete `if (j < lo) j = lo;` -> both new tests red (and the golden test);
- delete the refusal `return { why: ... }` line -> refusal test red;
- drop the `j <= hi` half of the refusal condition -> refusal test red (inch case);
- drop the `j - jRec < 1` half -> refusal test red (mm case).

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites 5 s, app suites 1648 s - the shared golden pulled every app suite). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder --test lathe_post_tormach_thread -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a PathPilot / LinuxCNC run of the new inch golden; no batch gate (budget).

## Overlaps

- #517 and #518 (G76 on both lathe posts): `git merge-tree` with each branch is clean (#517 changes `g76Why`, this changes `g76Grid`), so not stacked. With #517's finish-allowance rule the record's rung count is still ceil(height / first depth).
- #1667 and #1681 conflict with this on adjacent lines of the same inch golden and `lathe_post_tormach_thread.rs` (their G30 / drive-line changes next to the G76 line): a mechanical keep-both, regenerate the golden at merge.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1619-g76-inch-ladder.md`.

Fork synced at v0.19.0 (branched from upstream/main 058e14ca).

Changelog: Tormach lathe G76 (inch) states a first depth J whose LinuxCNC R1 ladder cuts exactly the verified passes (J0.0315, not 0.0314, on the M12x2 fixture); a record no grid J can state is refused by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1619

title: fix(import): load a STEP closed shell that meshes open as an incomplete model
body:
## What changed

A STEP closed shell that meshes open (a real gap, e.g. walls missing on a face truck cannot mesh) used to be refused at import (#1576), so the part could not even be loaded for viewing or setup. Now the model import lands it **incomplete**:

- `step_closed::judge` returns the hole, named, instead of refusing; `step::parse_open` and `import::{load,parse}_model_open_within` keep it in `Graded::open`. Every other loader (`load_model`, `parse_model`, `*_graded_within`: fixtures-by-path, tool bodies) still refuses with the same words as before.
- `ImportModel` (GUI, MCP `import_model`, script `import`) lands the mesh with the fidelity-unknown sentinel (`model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM`, #1056) and the hole in a new component `schema::MeshOpen`. The sentinel rides every chord path (stock copies, setup clones, undo, save), so every operation on the model and the program verdict are refused at the post by the existing gate, and the program sim gives no verdict.
- New module `mesh_open`: the refusal words ("model 'X' was imported incomplete - closed shell #N (F faces) meshes open: ... - so it has walls missing and no gouge check against it can be trusted; re-export the model, or import an STL"), the model page / import status line ("Incomplete: ..."), and the MCP/script `reduced_fidelity` facts (`incomplete: true`, `hole`).
- The hole is traded by `UpdateModel` (new `with_hole`, undo restores it; a whole re-import clears it), `DeleteEntity` undo, and the project file (optional entity key `mesh_open`, written only beside `fidelity_unknown`; a `mesh_open` without the mark is refused as corrupt). No project version bump: an old reader drops the key and keeps the mark, so it still refuses (decision file).
- `model_fidelity::set` clears any hole, so a stale hole never speaks for a whole mesh.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1610-open-shell-incomplete.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, new suite `crates/app/tests/import_step_open_shell.rs`:
- `a_closed_shell_that_meshes_open_imports_incomplete_with_its_hole_named` (the bent `fillet_corner.step` fixture: loads, facets present, hole named incl. the dropped face, summary/facts say incomplete; the graded loader still refuses)
- `every_operation_on_an_incomplete_model_is_refused_at_the_post_naming_the_hole` (verification report, sim not judged, `post_setup` refused, not the pre-v59 note)
- `the_hole_rides_undo_and_a_whole_reimport_clears_it`
- `the_hole_rides_the_project_file_and_is_refused_without_its_mark`

Updated: `step_seams_tests::the_importer_closes_seams_within_two_chord_tolerances_only` (the gap is now returned named, not refused, by `judge`).

Mutation checks (each line deleted or neutralised, the two STEP suites run, restored and touched): 17 of 17 red - `MeshOpen` write, the hole in `op_problem` / `verdict_tol` / the fixture line, save / load / validate of `mesh_open`, `ImportModel`'s unknown chord, hole landing and `graded.open`, `UpdateModel` apply and undo, `DeleteEntity` undo, the parser collecting holes, `judge` returning the hole, and both graded loaders still refusing.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): green on 35b3422c (app suites 364 s, ui suites 151 s). Clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The model page and status line in the running GUI (no screenshots; the text comes from `mesh_open::summary`, pinned).
- The user's real-world STEP files that motivated #1576 (local only, not committed).
- A stock copied from an incomplete model whose source is then deleted: still refused, but its refusal falls back to the pre-v59 words (noted in the decision file).

Branched from upstream/main 058e14ca. Process change: no.

Changelog: A STEP closed shell that meshes open now imports as an incomplete model with its hole named, instead of being refused; every operation on it is refused at the post by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1610

title: fix(kernel): meter truck's faces in the STEP bench so a runaway face is refused
body:
## What changed

- The release gate of the v0.20.0 cut stopped in `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name` on `testdata/models/bspline_discontinuous.step`.
- Cause: the solidcore reader and the solidcore mesher answer on that file in a few milliseconds (probe run, debug). The bench's own truck reader (`truck_read` in `crates/kernel/tests/step_util/mod.rs`) called `robust_triangulation` with no meter. truck's subdivision does not end on a B-spline that is not continuous. truck reads no cancel token. Thus the time bound had no effect, and the test thread did not stop.
- Fix: the new file `crates/kernel/tests/step_util/truck_guard.rs` wraps each face in a metered surface. This is the bench copy of the meter that crates/app uses since #1536 (25 M evaluations for each face). The meter also reads the bench's cancel token. After the cap or the cancel, the bench refuses the file by name, for example `shell #17: face 6 of 6 (B-spline surface) not meshed: its subdivision did not converge within the evaluation cap`.
- `truck_read` now takes the cancel token. `step_agreement.rs` and `step_import.rs` give it.
- Three fixtures had no verdict row in `step_agreement.rs`. They now have rows: `bspline_discontinuous.step` (both refuse), `bspline_dome.step` (agree, mesh volume off: a FINDING on solidcore-tess), `fillet_corner.step` (solidcore refuses).
- New dev-dependency: `truck-topology` (workspace pin, already in the graph through crates/app). truck-stepio does not re-export `CompressedShell`. No `camcraft-*` edge. The library is not changed. Decision: `docs/decisions/1697-bench-truck-guard.md`.

## How tested (debug, Windows)

- `step_agreement`: 1 passed in 10.1 s. Before the fix, the test failed at its 90 s bound.
- `step_import`: 4 passed, with the new pinning test `truck_side_refuses_a_runaway_face_and_obeys_its_cancel`.
- `solidcraft_hostile` 3 passed, `solidcraft_import` 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The kernel suites in release mode, and the release lane `mesh_deviation_bench` (it uses its own fixture list, and this change does not touch it).
- Linux and macOS.

Changelog: none
Effort: high

Fixes #1697

title: fix(ui): keep the near plane and the ortho eye consistent with the zoom
body:
### Summary

A viewport fix for the way the camera eats the model from the inside.

Two ways the camera clipped the model while zooming:

- **Perspective:** the near plane was a fixed 0.1 mm from the eye, so at close zoom the geometry right in front of the near plane clipped instead of rendering — zooming in went through the model. The near plane now rides `dist` (0.1 % of the view depth, clamped to 1e-5 min and 0.1 max).
- **Orthographic:** `dist` moved the eye, so zooming dollied the eye into the model and clipped through its faces from inside. The eye now sits at a fixed nominal distance (100 mm) behind the target, and `dist` is only a zoom factor for the view box's half-height — the way it was always meant to work.

The test pins the new near-plane formula (`(cam.dist * 0.001).clamp(1e-5, 0.1)`).

### Verification

`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` — 774 passed. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` is the maintainer's to dispatch; clippy clean.

title: fix(post): state the stock's turning radius on lathe streams
body:
Stacked on #1667 (the G30 logic of the Tormach lathe post). The diff shows the commits of #1667 until #1667 merges.

## What changed

- `Dump` in `camcraft-post` gets the field `stock_turn_radius`. When it is set, finite and more than 0, the stream gets `PARAM StockTurnRadius` after `StockZTop`.
- The new module `crates/app/src/stock_turn.rs` calculates the radius: the largest distance of a stock mesh vertex from the spindle axis (the world Z line through the setup origin).
- `posting.rs` sets the radius only for a lathe or mill-turn setup. Mill streams do not change.
- `tormach-lathe.cps`: `stockEnv()` uses the larger of the box half-width and `StockTurnRadius`. Thus the G30 approach and departure clear the rotating corners of a square bar.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` does not read the stock. It does not change.
- `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` gets a row for the new property.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/1666-stock-turn-radius.md`.

## Posted G-code changes

Yes, for a lathe program on a box (square bar) stock with the Tormach lathe post. The G30 departure goes to the corner diameter, not to the box width. A round bar gives the same radius as before, so its output does not change. No real control ran the output.

## Golden question (held for the maintainer)

Two goldens are stale on this branch. I did not regenerate them:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/axial_drill_mm.nc`: the last `G0 X24` becomes `G0 X33.941`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/axial_drill_inch.nc`: the same move in inch (`X0.9449` becomes about `X1.3363`).

The fixture uses a 24 x 24 box stock. The corners of the box turn on a circle of radius 16.971 mm (diameter 33.941). The new value is the correct clearance. Thus `lathe_post_tormach::an_axial_drill_posts_as_plain_moves_in_mm_and_inch` fails until the maintainer accepts the golden change.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_turn_radius.rs`:

- `a_lathe_stream_states_the_radius_its_stock_sweeps`
- `a_mill_stream_states_no_turning_radius`
- `the_g30_moves_use_the_square_bars_corner_circle`
- `a_square_bar_program_has_no_g30_rapid_inside_the_corners_circle`

All four pass. These suites also pass: `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_tormach_g30`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_workholding_mill_post`, `solid_law_goldens`, `tormach_lathes`, `turning_stock_approach` (camcraft-app), and `recorded_streams`, `post_engine`, `lathe_post_refusals` (camcraft-post). `lathe_post_tormach` has 7 of 8 pass; the failure is the golden above. title: fix(2d): name the stock band narrower than the tool around the part
body:
## What changed

A pocket-family operation (2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset) can clear the stock around the part. This occurs with a whole-model source (#12), or with the stock source when the setup holds parts (#1554). Before this fix, such an operation gave no pass to a band of that area narrower than the tool, and it gave no note. The outside of the part stayed uncut and nothing told the user.

Now the operation carries one note for those bands. The note gives:

- the operation kind,
- the tool diameter and the stock to leave,
- the XY box of each band,
- what to do: use a smaller tool, or a wider stock margin.

Example: `2D Adaptive: 1 band of the area to clear is narrower than the 10.000 mm tool, so no pass cuts it: X -35.000 mm to 35.000 mm, Y -35.000 mm to 35.000 mm - use a smaller tool, or a wider stock margin`

The cut does not change. A region where the tool reaches every piece gets no note, so no golden changes.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` (new): `unreached_pieces` and `unreached_note`. These pure functions find each connected piece of the region that erodes to nothing by the tool radius plus the stock to leave. They ignore noise slivers (narrower than 0.01 mm, or smaller than 1e-4 mm^2).
- `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`: `narrow_noted` adds the note for the pocket family only, and only when the operation clears around the part. The note never blocks the cut. If the band check cannot read the region, the path stays and a note says that the check did not run.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: one call after generation.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1655-narrow-band-note.md`. A note is used, not a cut past the stock edge. A cut past the stock edge would move every around-part pocket and its goldens. A follow-up issue can cut the band.

## Cause

`machining2d::pocket_entered` erodes the region by the tool radius plus the stock to leave. It refuses only a region that erodes to nothing as a whole. A connected piece that erodes to nothing gets no pass, and nothing reported it.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/narrow_band.rs`
  - `a_model_source_adaptive_names_the_outside_band_narrower_than_the_tool`: a 3 mm margin with a 10 mm tool. 2D Adaptive and 2D Pocket, with the part source and the stock source. The pocket in the part is cut, no pass is in the band, and one note names the band box.
  - `a_band_the_tool_fits_is_cut_and_says_nothing`: an 11 mm margin. The band is cut and no note is given.
- `camcraft-motion` unit tests `machining2d::unreached::law::*`: a band beside a wide bore, the stock to leave in the reach, a noise sliver, an empty region and a NaN reach.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` plan, run with `-j 4`): the motion suites and the app suites in the plan. Also `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Results: all motion suites pass; the app suites pass except `lead_approach` (2 tests). That suite fails the same way on the base without this change: it is #1675 (main is red after #1656). Clippy is clean. After a last edit (the note never blocks the cut), `narrow_band`, `keep_law` and `stock_source_law` ran again and pass.

## Not exercised

- A 3+2 tilted setup frame. The note box is in the local frame of the operation.
- Inch units (the format uses the same `units::len` path as the other notes).
- 2D Offset and the trochoidal method of 2D Adaptive: they use the same call site, but no test names them.
- The GUI. The note shows where the other operation notes show.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket, Adaptive or Offset that clears the stock around a part now names each band of the stock narrower than the tool, which no pass can cut (#1655)

Effort: high

title: fix(import): turn a closed STEP solid wound inward outward, and say so
body:
## What changed

- A STEP import now examines each body of the finished mesh (a body is a connected set of facets). A body that is closed, manifold, consistently wound and has a clearly negative signed volume is wound inward. The importer reverses each facet of that body, so the body turns outward.
- The verdict uses `pick::winding::winding_of`. The face picks use the same test. Thus the importer and the picks agree on what "inward" means.
- The importer does not change an open body (a lone face, a shell with a gap), a non-manifold body, a body with mixed winding or a body with no volume.
- The import tells the user about the change. `Graded::notes` and `ImportModel::notes` are new. The note goes to the MCP and script `import` result (`notes`) and to the status line.
- New module: `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_outward.rs`. `step.rs` does not change.

## Overlap

- PR #1576 adds the same `notes` plumbing for its flipped faces: `Graded`, `ImportModel`, `v_import`, `cam.d.ts`, `script/mod.rs`, the MCP description and the status line in `ui/src/state.rs`. Where possible, the code lines here are the same as the lines in #1576. The second PR to merge must keep one copy of the plumbing. In `parse_model_graded_within`, it must keep both note sources (the #1576 face notes and the `step_outward` note).
- PR #1638 changes `step.rs` and the module list in `import/mod.rs`. This PR does not change `step.rs`. It adds `mod step_outward;` at a different line of the module list.

## How tested

- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_outward_tests.rs` (unit): an outward cube, an inward cube, two bodies with one inward, a lone curved face (both windings) and a mixed cube.
- `crates/app/tests/import_step_outward.rs`:
  - `an_inward_closed_box_is_turned_outward_and_said`: `box.step` with all senses reversed imports with the same positive volume as the plain box, and with one note.
  - `a_lone_curved_face_is_left_alone`: the B-spline face of `bspline_dome.step` alone in an `OPEN_SHELL`, in both windings. No note, and each keeps its own winding.
  - `the_mcp_import_result_carries_the_note`: the MCP `import_model` result has `notes` for the inward box and no `notes` for the plain box.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/import_outward.rs`: `an_inward_solid_is_turned_and_said_on_the_status_line`.
- All of the tests above pass on head 8926917.
- These suites also pass: the `camcraft-app` lib tests that match `import`, and `import_step_guard`, `mcp`, `model_fidelity`, `scripting`, `step_budget`, `step_chord_units`, `step_fidelity`, `step_nesting`, ui `models` and ui `fixtures`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(motion): bore-side Contour ramp entry holds the ramp angle
body:
Branch base: upstream/main 2b6e03f2.

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_bore.rs`, the `Entry3D::Ramp` arm (no entry ramp angle set):
  - The single chord stays only when it is not steeper than the links' ramp angle (3 deg by default).
  - On a closed ring, the chord has no run. In that case, or when the chord is steeper, the ramp zig-zags along the lead-in and the ring at that angle. It uses the same `plan_zig_capped` and `push_zig` as the entry-angle arm.
  - When the path is too short for the angle, the descent substitutes by name ("the lead-in and ring are too short to ramp at the angle"). This is an axial dive at the plunge feed with an `entry:` note.
  - A blocked chord substitutes by name, as before.
  - Side Outside does not change.
- New helpers in the same file: `level_angle`, `within_angle`, `zig_onto`. The entry-angle arm now uses `zig_onto` too. Its output does not change.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1664-contour-inside-ramp.md`.

## Pins

New suite `crates/motion/tests/contour_inside_ramp.rs`:
- `a_bore_side_ramp_entry_contour_never_descends_steeper_than_its_ramp_angle`: the issue repro, climb and conventional. Each descending feed move is at most 3 deg, or an axial move at the plunge feed with an `entry:` note. This ring has room, so there is no dive.
- `a_bore_side_ring_too_short_to_ramp_dives_by_name_at_the_plunge_feed`: `ramp_max_len` 0.1. Each level dives by name at the plunge feed.

## Mutation checks

title: fix(verify): a Face row through a rim vertex crosses the rim
body:
## What changed

A stock-source Face got a false `Gouge` on its last row when that row was tangent to the stock edge. The row was above the stock top and the document had no part. The post refused the program (#1659).

**Root cause.** The stock outline has vertices on its straight sides: `(62, 60)`, `(-2, 60)`, `(0, 62)` and `(0, -2)`. The last row (`(-4, 60) -> (64, 60)`) goes exactly through `(-2, 60)` and `(62, 60)`. The Boundary wall reading of law (b) with no model (`wall_gouge` in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs`) excuses a row that crosses the rim. But it counted only a proper crossing through the interior of an edge. A row through a vertex crossed no edge interior. Thus the law read it as a move in the region, at distance 0 from the vertex, and gave `Gouge { at: 42 }`. The first row (y 0) got no warning because no vertex is on its line. The cause was not the keep law of #1607, the stock sim or a tolerance sign.

**Fix.** A new helper `crosses_rim` (`section.rs`) also counts a pass through a loop vertex when the two neighbours of the vertex are on opposite sides of the trace (`Trace::through` in `crates/sim/src/verify/arc_wall.rs`, for a segment, an XY arc and an XZ / YZ footprint, within `CROSSING_TOUCH`). A touch at a vertex (both neighbours on one side) is not a crossing and stays a gouge. No tolerance changed; `GOUGE_TOL` stays 0.01.

## How tested

Pins, each mutation-checked:

| Pin | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| app `face_stock_edge::a_face_row_tangent_to_the_stock_edge_in_air_with_no_part_is_clean_and_posts` (the issue's exact repro, move 42, posts) | M1: no vertex crossing (the old law) | fails |
| sim `boundary_walls::a_row_through_two_side_vertices_tangent_to_the_far_edge_crosses_the_rim_and_is_clean` | M1 | fails |
| sim `boundary_walls::a_move_inside_or_only_touching_a_vertex_still_answers_to_the_walls` | M2: every vertex a crossing | fails (and the #43 corner pin fails too) |
| app `face_stock_edge::the_same_face_over_a_part_whose_top_stands_above_cut_z_is_refused` | M5: keep law gets no parts | fails |
| app `face_stock_edge::a_tangent_last_row_0_02_mm_into_a_part_is_refused` (only the last row is convicted; the post stops) | M3: `GOUGE_TOL` 0.03; M5 | fails |

With the fix, all pins pass. Note: M4 (laws b and b2 off in the sim verifier) does not break the two part pins. The keep law in the operation layer convicts them.

Gates:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (sim lib, `boundary_arc_planes`, `boundary_arc_walls`, `boundary_walls`, `model_excess`; app `coarse_rims`, `face_stock_edge`, `real_tip_contour`, `slot_caps`, `thread_mill_rim`, `verify_arc_reading`).
- Also run: app `area_controls`, `area_open`, `stock_source_law`, `after_op`, `accessory_collisions`, `post_not_judged`: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- The batch and release tiers, and the GUI.
- The arc branch of `Trace::through` has no direct pin. A Face row is a straight move.
- I did not find why the stock outline carries vertices on its sides. A vertex on a straight side is a correct loop, so the verifier now reads it correctly (see the decision file).

Decision: `docs/decisions/1659-face-rim-vertex-crossing.md`.

Fork synced at v0.18.0; branch made from `upstream/main` (2b6e03f).

Changelog: A Face on the stock whose last row is tangent to the stock edge, with no part, no longer gets a false Gouge and posts (#1659).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1659

title: fix(motion): circular ramp entry rides the ring at the ramp angle
body:
## What changed

A Circular with `entry: ramp` did not ramp at its ramp angle. The cause is the legacy ramp chord. The chord goes from the tool's XY to the pass start. A ring starts and ends at the same point. Thus at each level change the chord has no length: the tool fed straight down at the cutting feed (500), with no note. The first entry of the inner ring was a 76 deg chord from the outer ring. The first entry of the outer ring was an axial dive.

The fix is one match arm in `descent::plan_arm` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs`). On the circular kernel (`Motion::ring_zig`), the Ramp arm now plans the zig-zag ramp along the ring. It uses `ramp_fallback`, the same path as the helix's stand-down. The angle is the transition's ramp angle (3 deg by default). The ramp rides the ring's arcs (`push_zig_ring`, #1558). If the ring is too short for the angle, the descent is a dive at the plunge feed with the note `entry: the ring is too short to ramp at the angle - axial dive on the floor instead at (...)`.

The arm applies only to the circular kernel. Other ladders (pocket, contour, bore) do not change. This change does not touch `ring.rs` (no overlap with PR #1651).

Decision: `docs/decisions/1609-circular-ramp-angle.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/motion/tests/circular_ramp_angle.rs`, on the #1558 repro with `entry: ramp`, climb and conventional:
- `a_ramp_entry_circular_never_descends_steeper_than_its_ramp_angle`: each descending feed move is at most 3 deg (measured along the arc), or it is an axial move at the plunge feed with an `entry:` note.
- `every_ring_level_of_the_ramp_entry_is_entered_by_the_ramp`: no axial descent on this hole.

Both tests are red on upstream main (an axial feed at 500 at (-34.0, 2.9, -1.508); 25 axial descents).

Mutation checks (each one red, then reverted):
- The arm always substitutes: both tests red.
- The substitution dives at the cutting feed: both tests red.
- `ramp_fallback` doubles the angle: the angle test red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (motion lib, center_cut_law, circular_ramp_angle, entry_approach, level_links, predrilled_entry, xy_arc_entry; app bore_entry, ladder_entry_height). Also green: motion `circular_arcs`; app `arc_entry`, `circular_arcs`, `circular_pick_law`, `circular_entity_law`, `circle_centre`, `circular_pick`, `golden_cl`, `mill2d_b`, `operations`, `pocket_recognition`, `units_in_refusals`, `stock_source_law`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens

No golden moves. No committed golden uses a Circular with `entry: ramp` (`circular_ring_arcs.cl` uses Helix; `sinker_orbit_circular.cl` is the sinker orbit). Posted G-code of a Circular with `entry: ramp` changes: the straight feeds and the steep chord become helical ramp arcs at 3 deg.

## Not exercised

- Other ladders with closed passes (pocket offset rings, bore) and a Ramp entry with no angle set: not checked for the same straight chord.
- Batch and release tiers.

Changelog: Circular with entry Ramp now ramps along the ring at the ramp angle (3 deg by default) at every level, or dives at the plunge feed with a note; before, it fed straight down at the cutting feed (#1609)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at upstream/main 2b6e03f2.

Fixes #1609

title: fix(motion): open the trochoidal slot's bore on a band wider than the tool radius
body:
## What changed

- `plan_trochoidal_slot` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/trochoid_slot.rs`) now asks the lane planner for the opened bore (`trochoid_bore::bore` with `open: true`, from #1509) when the loop band's half-width `b` is more than the tool radius `r`.
- Cause: a helix of radius `b` clears only the ring `b +- r`. When `b > r` (a channel wider than twice the tool), the plain bore left a post of radius `b - r` at the start, at full depth. No front arc reached it, and the operation reported OK.
- When `b <= r`, the slot keeps the plain bore, and the output does not change.
- The doc comment of `trochoid_bore.rs` now gives the new rule.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1589-troch-slot-open-bore.md`.

## How tested

- `trochoid_wide_channel_leaves_no_post_at_the_start` (motion `tests/trochoid_slot.rs`): D 10, W 26 (b 8, r 5). The rest area in a 2.5 mm disc about the start is 0.000 mm2, and the measured engagement is 78.0 deg (limit 90). With the plain bore forced, the same test fails with 19.72 mm2 standing.
- `the_opened_bore_leaves_no_post_at_the_lane_start` (motion lib, `adaptive_troch_tests.rs`), extended: the stand-alone slot on the #1509 band (b 4.5 to 5, D 6) leaves less than 0.5 mm2 and holds the engagement limit.
- `a_slot_band_within_the_tool_radius_keeps_the_plain_bore` (motion lib): W 10 and W 12 with D 6 give a path equal to the plain-bore plan, move for move.
- The golden `trochoid_slot_small.cl` (app `golden_cl`) does not change.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: motion suites and app suites are green (12.3 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## What was not exercised

- The GUI was not started.
- No deep-stepdown test on a wide slot. The opened helix has half the tool radius, so it needs more turns. A very deep stepdown can now hit the helix turn cap. That case is refused by name ("half the tool radius - use a smaller stepdown").
- The release-lane heavy suites were not run.

Changelog: Trochoidal slot: a channel wider than twice the tool no longer leaves a post standing at its start; the bore now spirals out to the loop band.

Effort: high (no escalation)

body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/carvera.cps`: after `M6 T..`, the Carvera now writes `G0 Z<ClearancePlane|RetractPlane>` (never below the move's Z) before the first `G0 X.. Y..`. This is the same order as at a program start. The X/Y-first branch (`changedAt`) is removed. The provenance header and the note before `xyFirst` cite the firmware source.
- `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance.rs`: the X/Y-first case is removed. Two new pins:
  - `the_carvera_states_the_clearance_before_any_xy_after_its_m6`
  - `the_carvera_script_cites_where_its_m6_leaves_the_spindle` (replaces `the_carvera_script_names_the_open_hazard_after_its_tool_change`)
- `docs/decisions/1616-carvera-after-m6.md`: the decision, the sources and the options that were dropped. It supersedes the Carvera part of `docs/decisions/1616-first-traverse-clearance.md` (PR #1632).

## Sources (public GPL source, behaviour only; no vendor binaries, no decompiling)

- MakeraInc/CarveraFirmware `6e12557cfa5eff446bb5fe014354eaa03abf0caa`, `src/modules/tools/atc/ATCHandler.cpp`, `on_main_loop`: at the end of `M6`, the firmware does a machine rapid to `Z = coordinate.clearance_z`, then a rapid to the X/Y that it saved when `M6` arrived. The spindle is not left over the tool rack.
- Carvera-Community/Carvera_Community_Firmware `2c97111cb0bbd6d3edfac2c138963c0255248865`: the same order.
- `Robot.cpp`: the soft Z limit is on by default and halts the machine. A `G0 Z` that cannot be reached stops the program.

The diff shape is the same in every file: two lines after each `M6` change places. No line is added or removed. `two_tool_pocket.nc` has two `M6` blocks; all other files have one.

title: fix(motion): a chord that grazes one piece's wall and leaves the area no longer clears
body:
## What changed

- `chord_clears` moved from `slots.rs` to the new `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chord_clear.rs` (`slots.rs` re-exports it).
- The law splits the chord at each loop vertex that the chord touches without a crossing. The midpoint of each piece must be in the closed region. Before, one midpoint decided the full chord.

## The cause

The part pinches the band between the part and the stock. Thus, the cutter-centre area has pieces whose walls are on one line (Y -32, the offset edge of the stock). The old law found no edge that crossed the chord from (-8.05, -32) to (32, -32), and it read one midpoint, which was in a piece. Thus, the 2D Adaptive path fed along Y -32 at each level, 0.94 mm into the part.

The issue gives "10 mm at (-1.44, -29.94)". That value comes from the stock in the first report: its top is at Z 10, and the top of the part is at Z 20. The sim reads each part column above the stock as a 10 mm gouge, and (-1.44, -29.94) is the first part column. The pin uses a stock that covers the part.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/adaptive_pinch.rs`:
  - `a_whole_model_clearing_never_joins_two_corners_across_the_part_that_pinches_them`: a 20 mm disc in a 31 mm stock. 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset, aligned and turned stock. The cutter stays off the disc, and the op has no warnings.
  - `the_users_part_with_default_adaptive_keeps_the_cutter_off_it` (heavy lane, about 5 min in debug): `Milling-test.step` in a 70 x 70 x 27 box on Z -7, 2D Adaptive seed params, through `GenerateOperation` (`operation::generate`). Aligned and turned stock: the cutter reaches less than 0.06 mm into the part section at each Z, and the op has 0 warnings. Aligned stock: `simulate_document` has 0 gouge cells.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chord_clear.rs`: two unit tests (a chord across the gap between two pieces does not clear; a graze along one wall clears).
- Mutation: with the old midpoint law, all three pins fail ("reaches 0.936 into the part" at (1.963, -32.000, 15.000); "0.479 into the disc"; the gap chord clears). A first draft also split the chord at the ends of collinear edges. With that branch removed, all pins pass, so I removed it (the vertex split does that work).
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion suites 145 s, app suites 209 s, 0 failed). It includes `golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens`. No golden moved.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The pin uses an end mill with 30 mm flutes. With the catalog's 15 mm flutes, the 25 mm deep part gives `ShankHit` warnings at the lower levels. That refusal is correct and is not part of this issue.
- The sim pin runs only on the aligned stock. The program sim does not run on the turned stock; the op check covers it.
- The keep law of #1615 is not on main, so this PR does not run it.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1620-chord-pieces.md`.

The branch is based on c00ba18a and merges upstream/main 3ead1295.

Changelog: A 2D clearing no longer feeds across the part between two pieces of the cutter area whose walls are on one line (whole-model 2D Adaptive on Milling-test.step cut 0.94 mm into the part).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1620

title: fix(2d): judge a part-source cross drill against the setup's other parts
body:
**Stacked on #1640** - review only after 1e92ae6c (#1640's head after its refresh); merge #1622, #1634, #1640 first. #1615 is merged. (Fork synced at v0.18.0; branch based on #1640's head da340c0f, then #1640's refresh 1e92ae6c merged in at a60e6c3d.)

## What changed

#1621's neighbour law (`keep_law::neighbour_parts`) judged a part-source op against the setup's OTHER parts only when `depth_law_of` was not `None`. A Drill with cross holes reads `None` (its part law is the radial `cross_part`), so its neighbour set was empty, and the program sim does not judge a posed (radial) chain.

- `keep_law::kept_models` now includes a part-source cross drill (`is_cross_drill`): the setup's parts but the source, fixtures and a stock-only model left out.
- `cross_spindle::Solids` gains `neighbours`. After the source's own `cross_part::part_clear`, the new `cross_part::neighbours_clear` sweeps the finished chain (drill, shank, holder, rapids, posed along each move's axis) against those parts with **no hole wall excused**, on and off the work offset, and refuses by name.
- A stock-source cross drill passes no neighbours (#1635 already judges every part in its stock).

## Readings (reproduced first, on da340c0f)

Mill-turn bench, B = the #117 r10 punched bar with its r2 cross hole modelled (legal for B), A = a box; r20 bar and 40 x 40 box stocks, aligned and turned a quarter about Z; op on source "B".

| case | before (all four stocks) | now |
|---|---|---|
| A x [12, 18] across the drill's line, no hole in A | generates clean, **posts** | refused: "cross hole at (10, 0, 0) along (-1, 0, 0) cuts into a neighbouring part: another part the setup holds stands in the drill's line or its approach ..."; nothing written |
| A outside the raw bar, in the approach only | - | refused by name, aligned and turned |
| A a tube whose r3 32-gon bore sits on the line (B's r3 hole at size) | - | refused (a neighbour's wall is never excused) |
| A on B's far side, or 2 mm over the drill | posts | posts |

So it was a real P1: a gouge of part A posted unjudged on both stocks.

## How tested

Pins in `crates/app/tests/cross_drill_neighbours.rs`:
- `a_cross_drill_on_b_into_part_a_is_refused_by_name_on_both_stocks`
- `a_cross_drill_whose_approach_crosses_part_a_is_refused_on_both_stocks`

- `a_cross_drill_on_b_clear_of_part_a_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `over_mcp_a_part_source_cross_drill_answers_for_the_neighbour_the_same` (MCP parity: `add_operation` with `"source": "B"`)

Mutations (each alone, then reverted; `stock_source_cross_drill.rs` also run):

| mutation | red |
|---|---|
| M1 cross drill out of `kept_models` (the old predicate) | into, approach, tube, MCP |
| M2 `neighbours_clear` not called | into, approach, tube, MCP |
| M3 source's hole walls excused on the neighbours | tube |
| M4 2D tail's neighbour law skipped for a cross drill | none - so no guard was added; the tail's law stays on as a second net |
| M5 part-source arm passes no neighbours | into, approach, tube, MCP |

## Not exercised

A plain lathe holding two parts; the 3+2 frame arm (a cross drill is lathe / mill-turn work); MCP on a turned stock (`set_stock` takes no rotation).

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1641-cross-drill-neighbours.md`.

title: fix(2d): judge the parts beside an op's source again live at the post
body:
Stacked on #1622 (branch `issue/1607-stock-source-law`; the `keep_law::parts_in_stock` / `neighbour_parts` code exists only there). Fork synced at v0.19.0.

## What changed

Since #1603 / #1607 / #1621 an operation is judged against parts BESIDE its source, but those parts are not in its stamp. A part moved into the cut, added, or un-tagged as a fixture after a clean generation left the op `Ok`. On a turned stock (the program sim refuses to judge) the post read the cached clean verdict and posted into the part.

**Decision: option (c), no stamp term** (`docs/decisions/1628-kept-parts-live-judge.md`). When the program sim cannot judge, the post gate (`posting_sim`, not-judged arm) judges the parts again live:
- `operation::kept_rejudge::moved_part_problem` runs on each program op whose cached verdict is clean and whose kept part set is non-empty. It collects the op's job again and re-runs, on the cached path, the laws generation ran: the solid law (`contain_into`, `DepthLaw::Keep`), or the budgeted mark law for a stock-source Engrave/Trace. It uses the same cutter, stock to leave, excess and 3+2 frame, and the tap's core acquittal. It checks one kept part at a time, as each part stands now.
- A cut is refused by name: `stock sim did not judge this program: ... - and N1 now cuts part 'other' (move 328 cuts past the finish surface) - a part moved, added or no longer workholding since it was generated; regenerate it`.
- An op whose cached warnings already block is skipped, so it is still refused by its own findings, by name.
- On an aligned stock nothing changes: the sim already judges every part live.
- `generate::stock_to_leave_of`: the stock-to-leave table is moved out of `run_job_arms` unchanged, so both judges read one number. `contain_into` is now `pub(super)`. `keep_law::kept_parts_named` gives the kept set one mesh per model, by name.

Why not (a), the stamp term: it breaks the contracts the issue lists. With (c) they all pass unchanged on this branch: `fixtures::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath`, `operations::a_frommodel_stock_survives_its_source_being_deleted`, `operations::a_model_update_does_not_touch_a_box_stock`, `fidelity_copies` (both tests), and `stock_source_verdict`. All of these were in the quick gate.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/kept_parts_live.rs`, all on a turned stock)
- `a_neighbour_moved_into_a_part_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_is_refused_by_name`: a Trace on B is generated clean, then A is moved into its flank. The op stays Ok, and the post is refused naming `N1` and `other`. With A moved away again, the program posts.
- `a_part_added_into_a_stock_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_is_refused_by_name`: a stock-source Slot in the pocket is generated clean, then a boss is added under it. The op stays Ok, and the post is refused naming `S1` and `boss`.
- `a_fixture_untagged_then_moved_into_a_part_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_is_refused_by_name`: the clamp is tagged, then untagged. The op stays Ok (the M2.3 law) and the program posts. The clamp is then moved into the cut and the post is refused naming `clamp`.
- `a_part_moved_into_a_stock_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_never_posts`: moving the part under a stock-source op already stales it (another stamp input), so the post is refused with "regenerate".

## Mutation checks (each line reverted, the test run red, then restored and touched)
1. The gate's `.or_else(|| kept_moved(..))` replaced with nothing: the 3 `kept_parts_live` refusal tests go red.
2. The refusal in `moved_part_problem` (`if let Some(w) = ... find(blocks_post)`) never taken: the same 3 go red.
3. The convicted-op skip in `kept_moved` deleted: red in `stock_source_law` (`engrave_and_trace_off_the_stock_...`, `the_typed_kinds_and_face_...`) and in `neighbour_law::a_cut_on_b_into_its_neighbour_...`. Without the skip, the by-name gouge refusal is displaced.
4. `marks` forced false (the mark law not used for a stock-source mark): red in `stock_source_law::a_legal_stock_source_cut_stays_clean_and_posts_on_both_stocks`. The re-judge would refuse a legal mark.

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/1607-stock-source-law` on 329db7d8: green (app suites 1227 s, ui suites 152 s, 0 failed). Clippy on `camcraft-app` (`--lib --tests -D warnings`) is clean.

## Not exercised
- 3+2 (tilted) ops: the cached world path is judged in the frame's local coordinates, as chords at the arc-fit tolerance. No suite has a clean tilted 2D op beside another part, so this arm is not covered by a test.
- The fail-closed arm for "the job cannot be collected again" is unreachable by any fixture: every input `collect_job` can fail on is a stamp input, so such an op reads Stale first.
- Un-marking raw-stock-only after generation goes through the same live set (`stock_source::judged`). It has no dedicated pin here.

Changelog: A part moved into, added to, or un-tagged inside an operation's cut after generation no longer posts on a turned stock: the post judges the parts beside each op's source again and refuses by name (#1628)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1628

title: fix(2d): judge a stock-source cross drill against the parts in its stock
body:
stacked on #1634 - review only after a3e9f32d (#1634's head after its refresh); merge #1622, #1634 first. #1615 is merged. (fork synced at v0.18.0)

## What was found (reproduced before any fix)

#1635 asked whether a stock-source cross drill that enters a part posts unjudged. It does not. `cross_part::part_clear` read the source's mesh, and off the stock that mesh is the stock itself. So EVERY stock-source cross drill was refused at generation, the illegal ones and the legal ones alike, with "cross hole ... rapids into the finished part". The stock was read as the solid to keep. Nothing reached the post, so this is not a P1. It is a false refusal of legal programs, which is P3 by the AGENTS.md table (left at P1 for the maintainer to lower).

Readings: #117 punched bar r10 with one r2 hole plunging -X from (10, 0, 0), 6 mm deep. Stocks: an r20 bar and a 40 x 40 box, each aligned and turned a quarter about Z. Mill-turn and lathe benches. Stock-source op S1.

| case | before (all four stocks) | now |
|---|---|---|
| hole where the bar models none | refused: "rapids into the finished part" (meaning the stock) | refused: "cuts into the finished part: the drill meets steel at the mouth - the model has no hole there" |
| into the bar's modelled hole | refused, same words | generates the part source's chain, move for move; posts |
| stock-only material (r3 core) | refused, same words | generates; posts |
| lathe, box stock, legal hole | refused: "cannot be read as turned" (that is the box) | generates |

## What changed

- `cross_spindle::cross_drill` takes `Solids { source, stock, kept }`.
  - On a part source: unchanged (the part, the setup's stock, the part).
  - On a stock source: the setup's parts are the solid it measures and keeps, and the source stock is the raw material its mouths stand off. This is exactly the chain a part-source cross drill drills in that stock.
- `keep_law::is_cross_drill` joins `is_stock_kept_kind`, so `parts_in_stock` returns the setup's parts for it. Fixtures and a stock-only model are left out.
- The 2D tail's vertical solid law against those parts skips a cross drill (`parts_crossed`). The radial law has already judged the chain, and the solid law with no wall excuse would convict a drill sized to a faceted cross hole.
- On a plain lathe, a stock-source cross drill reads the parts as the turned work, not the box stock.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1635-stock-cross-drill.md`.

## How tested

Pins in `crates/app/tests/stock_source_cross_drill.rs` (new):
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_into_the_part_is_refused_by_name_on_both_stocks`
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_into_the_parts_own_hole_or_stock_only_material_posts` (also asserts the chain equals the part source's)
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_at_the_modelled_holes_size_is_excused_its_faceted_wall`
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_with_no_part_in_the_setup_keeps_nothing`
- `a_lathe_reads_the_turned_part_in_a_box_stock_not_the_box`
- `over_mcp_a_stock_source_cross_drill_answers_for_the_part_the_same` (built-in Mill-turn, MCP's default Stock source)

Six mutations, each checked red and then reverted. The table is in the decision file.

Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on da340c0f: sim 102 s, motion 6 s, app 1262 s, ui 59 s, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The 3+2 frame arm's `parts_crossed` guard. A cross drill is lathe or mill-turn work and does not reach that arm.
- A posted program on a plain lathe. The bench mounts no turning post.
- MCP on a turned stock. MCP's `set_stock` takes no rotation.

## Follow-up

A part-source cross drill still answers only to its own source, not to #1621's neighbouring parts.

Changelog: A cross drill taken off the stock is judged against the parts the stock holds, not against the stock: drilling a part's own cross hole off the raw bar now generates and posts, and a hole into a part where it models none is refused by name (#1635).
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1635

title: feat(ui): the CamCraft UI workbench rework
body:
### Summary

CamCraft's UI gets its workbench rework, built on upstream v0.19.0. It gives the shell a light workbench theme (`horizon-day`), puts a tab row above the ribbon cells to switch machine modes in one click, gives the operation page's section tabs their own glyphs, tightens the browser's chrome and row order, and adds camera tools to the viewport's floating control ribbon.

Refs #1677 (the workbench rework track; follow-up #1678 removes the unreachable Machine-door code).

Changelog: UI — changed the density of the built-in themes' shipped tokens: `cell_h` 40 -> 30, `cell_w` 72 -> 76, `glyph_px` 24 -> 16, `font_label` 13 -> 11, kept so the ribbon's caption row still fits the tab strip; the ribbon height stays 66 px (`RIBBON_TAB_H + cell_h + 20.0`). Pointer tests re-anchored to the compacted browser header. Horizon Day opts into the same density and the light palette.

Five commits, one topic each:

- `feat(ui): a light workbench theme and workspace tabs`
- `feat(ui): the operation page's section tabs wear their own glyphs`
- `feat(ui): a compact browser header and ordered rows`
- `feat(ui): camera tools in the viewport's control ribbon`
- `refactor(ui): drop the Machine ribbon cell - the workspace tabs own the switch`

### Before (upstream f2b42e3d) / after (this branch)

Both windows show a fresh document at the same 100% size with the default dark theme and the default document: the 1280-point floor, 250% display scale.

![before: upstream v0.19.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahmetv10/Camcraft/feat/camcraft-ui/docs/images/pr-1639-workbench/before.png)

![after: this branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahmetv10/Camcraft/feat/camcraft-ui/docs/images/pr-1639-workbench/after.png)

### Density change to the built-in themes

Before this PR, the built-in dark and light columns shipped `cell_h` 40.0, `cell_w` 72.0, `glyph_px` 24.0 and `font_label` 13.0. They now ship 30.0 / 76.0 / 16.0 / 11.0, matching the Horizon Day accent's intended density. The ribbon height is unchanged at 66 px. The change is kept deliberately (a tighter default that still reads at 11 px), and is called out here rather than hidden in the token table.

### What to look at

- The ribbon gains a workspace tab row above the cells: one tab per machine mode in `machine_modes::MACHINE_MODES`, switching through the same undoable `LoadBuiltinMachine` the Machine door queued. The stocked door and the tabs were two doors onto one switch; the tabs won, and the SETUP group sheds the redundant "Machine" cell at the end. The Machine door's code path remains present but unreachable from the UI, tracked in #1678 for removal.
- `assets/themes/horizon-day.json` is a light "Horizon Day" palette (base light). Nothing switches the default theme; dark remains the default.
- The section tabs in the operation pages wear purpose-drawn `sec-*` glyphs (six SVG masters, rendered at the ribbon's token size; our own artwork); the ribbon cell ink gains a tinted-palette hook with a steel-blue tint for command glyphs.
- The viewport's floating control ribbon gains four buttons: a Perspective/Orthographic toggle (the View door's radios' true twin), and a latched Orbit/Pan/Zoom nav tool that owns the drag whatever the mouse button — a latched tool's click is no click at all.
- The browser heads with one chrome row (a View door, Expand all / Collapse all) and the setup's furniture leads the rows: Setups, WCS, Stock, Operations, Tool list, Fixtures, Machine, Post.

### Verification

`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` — 772 passed. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` — green (ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --lib --tests` — no warnings.

Known flake: the palette/assertion law tests are parallel-order dependent; a full parallel run can see a handful of them fail while `--test-threads=1` is all green. Serial runs pass. Nothing in this PR changes their behaviour; re-run to confirm.

Gate logs: `gate-logs/quick-20261114-*` (not committed).

title: fix(import): mesh rational B-spline thread strips closed and at full fidelity
body:
## What changed

The rational `B_SPLINE_SURFACE` faces of #1602's parts are thread flanks and roots. Each is one strip, degree 1 across and degree 2 along, in 36-degree arcs, about fourteen turns long. truck meshed each one into ~2 M facets with a 0.5-3 mm hole. Three causes, all fixed in the importer's wrapper around a face (`step_guard::Metered`), with truck itself unchanged:

1. **Facet runaway: the division split both directions.** truck's `parameter_division` flags BOTH intervals of a cell that fails its bilinear test. A strip curved only along v therefore gets 2^sweeps intervals across u. The new `step_division` tests each cell's iso-v chord (splits u) and iso-u chord (splits v) separately, and it falls back to truck's bilinear test (which splits both) only for a twist. Every cell of the result still passes truck's acceptance test. A division that is still splitting after 64 sweeps (a jump) spends the face's evaluation budget, so it is refused by name exactly as before (#1536). It never comes back as a grid with a wall in it.
2. **Slivers: the parameter plane was 350x too short across.** truck triangulates a trimmed face by constrained Delaunay in (u, v). With nothing to constrain the plane next to the boundary, the empty-circle rule joined boundary points to the far ends of the strip. The new `step_stretch` stretches the faster parameter of a B-spline/NURBS face by its mean-speed ratio, so the mesher's plane has about the same proportions as the face. A face within 4:1 is untouched.
3. **The hole: boundary points found on the wrong turn.** truck's no-hint presearch (a 51 x 51 grid) samples a 14-turn strip about three times a turn, and Newton then settles one pitch off, outside the knot domain. On a root band the extrapolated rulings meet other turns exactly, at u = 7 on [0, 1]. The new `step_nearest` re-searches any answer that is off the surface or outside the domain. It starts Newton from the nearest samples of a grid that has up to 4 samples in every knot span (<= 4,096 evaluations), and takes the nearest answer inside the domain. Poles are settled by `step_pole` first (#1548), as before.

Decision entry: `docs/decisions/1602-thread-strip-mesh.md`.

## Readings (release; the user's files stay local)

| File | upstream main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 10208.STEP | 6,095,454 facets, chord 0.0157 mm (reduced), 31-72 s | **13,662 facets, chord 0.005 mm, 1.9 s** |
| 32050.STEP | 4,970,604 facets, 62-130 s | **8,128 facets, chord 0.005 mm, 1.8 s** |
| sc_logo.step | 36,728 facets, 0.19 s | 34,496 facets, 0.19 s, 0 open edges |
| synthetic 14-turn flank (a scratch generator) | 7,540,126 facets, 248 s, 3.3 GB | 3,072 facets, 0.8 s |
| the test's 4-turn trimmed flank | 471,695 facets, 7.3 s | 861 facets, 0.08 s |
| testdata/models/*.step | | facet counts unchanged |

**Closed-shell check:** I trial-merged PR #1576's head (e7d78efe) locally, without pushing it. Both parts import closed and pass its check. Before this change that check refused them: 10208 at face #1073 (up to 3.0 mm) and 32050 at faces #3350 and #5466. The gaps #1576's check still reported on these files are this issue's faces, and they are gone now.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/import_step_thread.rs::a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_at_full_fidelity_in_a_bounded_count`: a STEP thread flank generated in the test (our own geometry, no user file), with run-out trims that cross the strip on the bias. It asserts fewer than 5,000 facets (471 K before), full chord, no triangle edge >= 2 mm, every facet within 0.01 mm of the ideal flank, and area within 1 % of the trimmed ideal.
- `step_division::tests`: `a_strip_curved_only_along_v_is_not_split_across_u`, `a_doubly_curved_patch_splits_both_ways`, `a_twist_the_chords_miss_still_splits_both_ways`, `a_jump_is_reported_as_not_converged`, `a_bad_tolerance_returns_the_corners`.
- `step_nearest::tests`: `a_point_on_a_many_turn_flank_is_found_on_its_own_turn`, `a_point_on_a_root_band_is_found_inside_the_knot_domain`, `a_point_off_the_face_keeps_trucks_answer`, `the_sample_grid_covers_every_span_within_its_bound`, `a_rescue_never_answers_outside_the_knot_domain`, `an_exact_answer_outside_the_domain_gives_way_to_one_on_the_surface_inside`, `a_nearer_answer_replaces_a_far_one_off_the_surface`.
- `step_stretch::tests`: `a_face_near_square_keeps_its_parameters`, `the_faster_direction_is_stretched_by_the_ratio`.
- `step_guard::tests`: `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane`, `a_metered_face_finds_boundary_points_on_their_own_turn`. The existing `a_discontinuous_bspline_division_stops_at_the_cap_and_trips_the_meter` and `nothing_keeps_running_after_a_refused_pass` still hold.

## Mutation checks

Each guard was broken by hand, the named test was run, and then the guard was restored (`git status` clean after each run):

| # | Guard broken | Test that went red |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | per-direction flags -> split both | `a_strip_curved_only_along_v_is_not_split_across_u` |
| M2 | twist fallback removed | `a_twist_the_chords_miss_still_splits_both_ways` |
| M3 | sweep cap returns the grid instead of `None` | `a_jump_is_reported_as_not_converged`, `a_discontinuous_bspline_division_stops_at_the_cap_and_trips_the_meter` |
| M4 | `meter.exhaust()` on no convergence removed | `a_discontinuous_bspline_division_stops_at_the_cap_and_trips_the_meter` |
| M5 | bad-tolerance guard removed | `a_bad_tolerance_returns_the_corners` (a hang, caught by its 20 s timeout) |
| M6 | stretch off (`Stretch::NONE`) | `a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_...` (a 12 mm triangle), `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane` |
| M7, M7b, M7c | u/v, second and mixed derivative scaling removed | `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane` |
| M8 | parameter range left unscaled | `a_stretched_face_shows_the_same_surface_in_the_mesher_plane` |
| M9 | rescue in `search_nearest_parameter` removed | `a_metered_face_finds_boundary_points_on_their_own_turn` |
| M10 | rescue in `search_parameter` removed | `a_metered_face_finds_boundary_points_on_their_own_turn` |
| M11 | out-of-domain answers no longer retried | `a_point_on_a_root_band_is_found_inside_the_knot_domain` |
| M12 | in-domain filter on candidates removed | `a_rescue_never_answers_outside_the_knot_domain` |
| M13 | "on the surface" clause removed | `an_exact_answer_outside_the_domain_gives_way_to_one_on_the_surface_inside` |
| M13b | "nearer" clause removed | `a_nearer_answer_replaces_a_far_one_off_the_surface` |
| M15 | stretch threshold 4 -> 1 | `a_face_near_square_keeps_its_parameters` |
| M16 | stretch cap 1e6 removed | `a_face_near_square_keeps_its_parameters` |

Not separately killable: replacing the selection guard with `if true` (always take the in-domain candidate). Taking it changes nothing unless Newton, started from in-domain samples, settles inside the domain farther from the point than truck's own answer. I found no fixture where that happens, because the runs go to the unconstrained nearest point and are then filtered out (M12). The guard stays as a defensive line.
An aspect-balancing pass that I tried during the work was dropped: its mutation left every test green, and the real files close without it.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: the app lib and 11 suites by gate map, among them `import_step_corner_blend` (#1548 pole), `import_step_guard`, `step_fidelity`, `step_budget` and `large_models`, plus the new `import_step_thread`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The `testdata/models/*.step` facet counts match upstream main, and `bspline_discontinuous.step` is still refused with the same message.

## Not exercised

- The heavy-lane `a_smooth_face_needing_more_than_the_old_cap_is_divided_not_tripped` (#1568, release `--ignored`) was not run.
- The UI import path was not run. The change is below `step::parse`, which every door shares.
- The real-file closure was checked only on a local trial merge with #1576, which is not on main.
- Windows and macOS were not run.

Changelog: STEP import meshes rational B-spline thread faces at full fidelity in seconds (about 10 K facets instead of 5-6 M per part, and no hole), splitting each parameter direction only where it is curved

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.19.0.

Fixes #1602

title: fix(post): Fanuc-family mill posts state the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

The second half of #1616 (PR #1632 did grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera; #1618 set the rule and wording on Tormach). `fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `sinumerik.cps` and `heidenhain.cps` no longer write the first move after `G43 H..` (or the TNC tool call) as one combined rapid from wherever the tool change left the tip. At the program's start and after every tool change, the first motion is preceded by:

1. a Z-only rapid to the section's `ClearancePlane`, else its `RetractPlane`, never below the move's own Z;
2. X/Y alone at that height (left out when the first rapid already is at that height - it is then the traverse itself);
3. for a feed, arc or probing move, a rapid down to the stream's start Z when that is lower;

then the move as the stream states it. A canned cycle read as the first motion is positioned over its hole at the stated height first. A stream that states neither plane is refused by name, and **the refused move is not written** - nor any later motion of that section while X/Y stay unknown (the rest of the section is refused cleanly; review of this PR), so no combined `G00 X.. Y.. Z..` from an unknown height reaches the program text. The wording is #1618/#1632's: `first X/Y traverse with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) - the post will not rapid X/Y at an unknown height` (prefixed `operation <name>: ` where the post knows it).

Each dialect writes its own rapid: `G00 Z..` (Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan), `G0 Z..` (Haas, 840D). The Heidenhain post is the TNC's ISO dialect, so its form is `G00 G40 G90 Z+..*` - the manual's own positioning block (the section's first motion block carries G40 G90), not `L Z.. FMAX`.

The issue's example, `synth_fanuc.nc`: `G00 X20 Y10 Z-3` after `G43 H02` is now `G00 Z5` / `G00 X20 Y10` / `G00 X20 Y10 Z-3`.

### Frame decision: G43.4 / TCP and rotary paths - correct in the frame, not refused

Recorded in `docs/decisions/1633-fanuc-first-traverse-clearance.md`.
- **Fanuc and Doosan, tilted first record (G43.4):** the rapids are written after the record's own `tilt()`, i.e. after `G43.4 H..` is armed. Z is then the tip's Z in the work offset - the frame the stream states its planes and words in. No rotary word rides the inserted blocks; the rotaries turn only on the record itself, at its target, as before.
- **Doosan indexing path (4th axis, no TCP):** the rapids are in G43 (the frame of the record's own words) with the table still clamped; the index (M11, the move, M10) is the record's.
- **Haas, Mazak, 840D, TNC:** they refuse tilted records (`tiltOk`), so the rapids are always upright.
- Dropped: refusing a tilted first record whose pose is unknown (every rapid of a real rotary program states its pose, so every 5-axis program would be refused at its start); writing the Z before the G43.4 arm (G43 is machine-Z length comp, so a tilted tip would not be at the stated height); inserting the Z line alone (the diagonal from clearance to a first target below the stock top would still cross the part).

## How tested

Pinning suite (new): `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family.rs`, #1632's five-test shape over all six posts plus four:
- `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z_first`
- `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated`
- `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` (also asserts no X/Y motion - neither the bare traverse nor the combined rapid - is written after the refusal, for every post)
- `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height`

title: fix(2d): judge a stock-source Chamfer, Drill, Bore or Thread against the parts in the stock
body:
**Stacked on #1622 - review only the commits after 4f0bfe7e (#1622's head after its refresh); merge #1622 first.** #1615 is merged. Fork synced at v0.19.0; branch made from #1622's head c74d888d, then #1622's refresh 4f0bfe7e merged in at a3e9f32d.

A stock-source 2D Chamfer, Drill, Bore or Thread stayed at `DepthLaw::None` (#1607 left them out of `keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind`), so a cut into a part held in the stock had 0 op findings: aligned, the program sim held the post; turned, **it posted**.

## What changed
- `keep_law::is_hole_kind` (new): Drill without cross holes, Bore, Thread. `is_stock_kept_kind` now holds these and `Chamfer2D`, so `parts_in_stock` collects the setup's parts for them (fixtures and a stock-only model left out, as #1607).
- `run_job`, both frame arms:
  - **Hole kinds:** the **containment law** against the parts (`contain_into` with `DepthLaw::Contain`). This is the law a part-source hole already answers to. It excuses only the round wall of each declared hole, measured about that hole's axis to the facets' sagitta (#1205), plus a thread mill's declared bore (#1071). A hole where the part models none, one wider than the part's hole, or one deeper than its floor is a blocking `Gouge`.
  - **2D Chamfer:** the **solid law** (`Keep`, nothing excused).
- **Tap core re-read (#266):** the closure that re-judges a Tap cycle's gouges at its core now also re-reads the stock-source parts and #1621's neighbours. Before, any gouge the core run did not raise was dropped. That run read only the source's own law, so those parts' gouges were acquitted without being checked. This is a #1622 gap fixed here because it shares the same lines. A part-source tap through a neighbouring lid that models no hole had 0 gouges before and is convicted now.

### Why the solid law for the Chamfer, not a mark-style budget
On a part source the chamfer breaks the part's own edge, which is legal by construction (#303 credits the declared break). Off the stock, the edge it follows is the **stock's** edge. A stock edge clear of every part meets no part facet, so the solid law finds nothing. A stock edge on or inside a part cuts a break into the part that no part edge declared. A mark-style budget (the part lowered by the chamfer depth) would allow a V-groove of that depth anywhere a stock edge crosses a part's face, which is the gouge this issue is about. The chamfer depth is also derived, not a number the user stated as permission. Cost: a chamfer off a stock **flush** with the part (box stock = the part's footprint) is now refused on the op, although the sim credits the break and it posted before. The workaround is to chamfer with the part as the source, which gives the same path and is legal there.

## Readings
Probe on c74d888d and on this branch. 30 x 30 x 20 plate with one modelled round hole; square box stock flush with its top, aligned or turned a quarter about Z.

| stock-source case | before: S1 gouges · aligned / turned | now: S1 gouges · aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|
| Drill Ø6 at (0, 9), no hole there / 3 mm under the r 3 hole's floor | 0 · refused by sim / **posts** | 1 · refused / refused by S1's moves |
| M6 Tap at (0, 9) / 3 mm past the Ø5 hole's floor | 0 · refused by sim / **posts** | 2 · refused / refused |
| Bore r 5 at (0, 9) / Bore r 6 in the r 5 hole | 0 · refused by sim / **posts** | 12 / 10 · refused / refused |
| Thread at (0, 9.5) / 4 mm under the hole's floor | 0 · refused by sim | 31 · refused (turned: never generates, #992) |
| Chamfer 1 mm, stock flush with the part | 0 · **posts / posts** | 5 · refused / refused |
| Part-source tap through a lid part (#1621 neighbour) | 0 | 2 |
| Drill / tap / bore / thread at the part's hole to size; the same at (25, 0) in stock-only material; chamfer on a 70 x 70 stock | 0 · posts | 0 · posts / posts (thread: aligned only) |

## Pins
`crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs` (6; fixtures in `stock_source_holes_support/`):
- `a_hole_kind_off_the_stock_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`: drill, tap, bore and thread, each both nowhere and too deep or too wide, on both stocks. The turned-stock thread is refused by name at generation.
- `a_hole_kind_in_the_parts_own_hole_or_in_stock_only_material_posts`: the part's hole is modelled as a 32-gon, so a tool at size passes only through the wall excuse.
- `a_chamfer_off_a_stock_flush_with_the_part_gouges_and_one_clear_of_it_posts`
- `a_tap_through_a_neighbouring_part_is_not_acquitted_at_its_core`
- `a_stock_source_hole_or_chamfer_with_no_part_in_the_setup_judges_nothing`
- `over_mcp_a_stock_source_hole_or_chamfer_answers_for_the_part_the_same`: MCP `add_operation` (default source: the stock), `generate`, `verify`. Drill into the part, in its hole and in stock-only material; chamfer flush and clear.

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | red |
|---|---|
| M1 the four kinds out of `is_stock_kept_kind` | into-part, chamfer, MCP |
| M2 hole kinds judged by the plain solid law | into-part, legal, MCP |
| M3 Chamfer out only | chamfer, MCP |
| M4 stock-source parts out of the tap core re-read | into-part (tap) |
| M5 neighbours out of the tap core re-read | tap-through-lid |
| M6 no thread bore granted against the parts | legal (thread) |
| M7 `Keep` instead of `Contain` (no wall excuse) | legal, MCP |

No existing test changed; no golden or snapshot changes.

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 881f7726 (sim 101 s, motion 5 s, app 1179 s, ui 48 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised
- The 3+2 frame arm with a stock-source hole or chamfer (same shape as #1607's arm).
- MCP on a turned stock (`set_stock` takes no rotation).
- A Thread off a turned stock never generates (#992's way-in law cannot read the program ahead there; this happens on a part source too). Pinned as it stands, not changed.
- The cross drill (a Drill with cross holes) on a stock source: its chain answers to `cross_part` against the source's mesh, not the setup's parts. Follow-up #1635 (P1).

Decision: `docs/decisions/1631-stock-holes-chamfer.md`.

MCP: no new command or tool; `add_operation` / `generate` / `verify` reach the law (pinned).

Changelog: A 2D Drill, Bore or Thread whose source is the stock is judged against the parts standing in that stock - it may enter a part only through the hole the part models there, to its size and depth - and a stock-source 2D Chamfer by the solid law, so a cut into a part is a blocking gouge on the operation and the post is refused even where the program sim cannot judge; a tap's core re-read no longer acquits a gouge in a neighbouring or stock-held part (#1631).
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1631
