title: fix(post): grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera state the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

The #1614 hazard in three more mill posts. After a tool change, and at the start of the program, `grblhal.cps`, `tinyg.cps` and `carvera.cps` used to write a bare `G0 X.. Y..` at whatever height the change left the tool tip. With a long tool on a high work offset, the tip can be below the part top at that height. grblHAL and TinyG now state that height, as `tormach.cps` does in #1618. The Carvera states it at a program start, but not before its first X/Y traverse after `M6` (see below):

- The traverse is at the section's `ClearancePlane`, or its `RetractPlane` when no clearance plane is stated. It is never below the move's own Z.
- **grblHAL and TinyG** write the Z-only `G0 Z` first, then the bare X/Y, then the descent.
- **Carvera (M3's option (c))** writes it in one of two orders:
  - Right after `M6 T..`: X/Y first, at the changer's exit height (main's order), then `G0 Z<clearance>`, then the descent. Nothing we have read says where the firmware parks X/Y after a tool change. A Z-only rapid down to a thin stock's clearance at that X/Y could meet the tools stored in the rack.
  - **The #1614 hazard stays for the Carvera after `M6`.** The bare X/Y traverse after `M6` is still made at the changer's exit height, and nothing we have read confirms that height. A long tool can leave the tip below the part top there, and the traverse then crosses the part. The hazard stays open until a public source confirms the firmware's `M6` exit position (option b). The comment in `carvera.cps` and the decision file say so.
  - At a program start with no tool change: Z first, like the other two posts.
- A stream that states neither plane is refused by name, with #1618's wording: "first X/Y traverse with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) - the post will not rapid X/Y at an unknown height". The operation name is added in front when the post knows it.
- When a feed is the first move, the existing rapid down to its start height is skipped if the traverse already went to that height. Before this change TinyG wrote that rapid every time.
- The planes are read per section and reset at the end of each section, as in #1618.
- The comments in all three posts that described X/Y first at the changer or safe height now match the code.

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` is not touched. #1618 and the #1626 branch own it.

`crates/app/tests/common/legacy_program.rs` gets the same hunk as #1618, line for line (checked by diff), so the two PRs merge cleanly. This is how the legacy goldens state their clearance from their `START` height.

**This PR does not close #1616 (`Refs #1616`).** Two parts of its "Done means" stay open: the Fanuc-family half (fanuc, haas, mazak, doosan-dnm, sinumerik, heidenhain), which is #1633, and the Carvera after `M6`. The Fanuc-family posts have no `xyUnknown` traverse; they write the combined first rapid after `G43`, and they carry G43.4 and rotary paths. I did not add the rule to `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: #1618 adds a bullet at the same spot, so editing it here would conflict. #1633 widens the bullet's list of posts. Option (c), the options considered and these choices are recorded in `docs/decisions/1616-first-traverse-clearance.md`.

## Moved goldens: 57 files, one added `G0 Z` line each (two in the two-tool programs)

I checked every moved golden by diff against `main`, not by a blanket regenerate. Each one gains only the clearance `G0 Z` line, and no line was removed or changed. A script confirmed where the added line sits:
- grblHAL and TinyG: right before the bare `G0 X.. Y..` traverse.
- Carvera: right after it, because each of these programs starts with `M6 T..`.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/{grblhal,carvera,tinyg}/` (12 legacy goldens each): `+G0 Z5`, or `+G0 Z6` for `drill_peck`. That is the golden's START or clearance height.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_{grblhal,carvera,tinyg}.nc`: `+G0 Z5`. The synth stream's ClearancePlane is 10 and OriginZ is 5.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/grblhal/altmill_4x4_two_tool{,_inch}.nc`: `+G0 Z15` (or `Z0.5906`) after each of the two tool changes.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/carvera/two_tool_pocket.nc`: `+G0 Z5` after `G0 X5 Y5` and again after `G0 X20 Y25`, after each `M6`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/{grblhal,carvera,tinyg}/{arcs,drill_retract,extreme_coords,full_circle,full_circle_raw}.nc`: `+G0 Z50`, or `+G0 Z10` for `drill_retract`.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/grblhal.nc`: `+G0 Z10` before the first `G0 X10 Y10`, which follows `G53 G0 Z0` / `T3 M6`.

In this round, the 19 Carvera goldens moved again: the `G0 Z` line now comes after the X/Y line that follows `M6`. On grblHAL and TinyG without `safe_retract`, the lift before the change already goes to the same work-offset height, so the added line repeats it. I kept it on purpose: the tool change itself (a manual change, a tool setter, a jog at TinyG's M0) can move Z.

## Tests

- Pinning suite `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance.rs`, run over all three posts on shipped machines (AltMill 2x4, TinyG 3-axis, Makera Carvera). Each post's traverse order is pinned: Z then X/Y, except Carvera after `M6`, which is X/Y then Z.
  - `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z`
  - `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated`
  - `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height`
  - `a_feed_first_move_rapids_down_from_the_stated_clearance`
  - `at_the_program_start_with_no_tool_change_the_clearance_z_comes_first` (new; all three posts, Carvera included)
- Existing tests whose streams stated no plane now state one, as `post::dump` does: `grblhal_post.rs`, `tinyg_post.rs`, `altmill_machines.rs`, `carvera_post.rs`, `post_spindle_rule_all.rs`. Two `G0 Z15` counts went up by the two stated traverses (grblhal 3 to 5, tinyg 5 to 7). The grblhal test now also checks that `G0 Z15` comes right before the `G0 X20 Y5` traverse.

**Mutation checks.** I mutated each post separately and ran the pinning suite. Every mutation turned it red:

| Mutation | Applied to | Tests that went red |
|---|---|---|
| M1: drop the `G0 Z<tz>` line | each post | 5 of 6 (all except the refusal test) |
| M2: replace the refusal with Z0 (`if (c === null) c = 0;`) | each post | `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` |
| M3: drop the same-height check | each post | `a_feed_first_move_rapids_down_from_the_stated_clearance` |
| M4: swap the order back to Z-first after `M6` (`if (changedAt)` changed to `if (false)`) | Carvera | 4 tests (tool change, retract plane, never below, feed first) |
| M5: X/Y first at program start too (`if (true)`) | Carvera | `at_the_program_start_with_no_tool_change_the_clearance_z_comes_first` |

After restoring the files, all 6 tests pass.

**Gate.** On a1833e52, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: post suites 22 s, app suites 1000 s, 0 failed. The change touches shared test input, so the quick tier ran nearly every app suite. The `import_step_guard` flake did not show. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No PathPilot Hub, grblHAL, TinyG or Carvera hardware or sender run. The output was read from the goldens only.
- The Carvera firmware's `M6` exit position (X, Y and Z) was not read from any documentation. That is why it gets option (c), and why the #1614 hazard stays open for the Carvera after `M6`.
- The Fanuc family is not changed; that is #1633.

Branched from upstream `main` at c00ba18a (fork worktree).

Changelog: grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera posts state the section's clearance Z (ClearancePlane, else RetractPlane) before the first descent after a tool change (Carvera: after its X/Y traverse at the changer's exit height, which stays unverified), and refuse a stream that states neither by name (#1616)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(ui): preserve document when opening a project fails
body:
Opening a malformed or semantically invalid project now keeps the existing document, history and filename on both disk and picked-byte paths. Each loader builds a replacement world first; only a successful load retires the old document. Successful opens preserve the user's theme and colour-vision preferences, and disk failures name the attempted file.

Validation:
- `refused_disk_project_keeps_document_and_history`
- `refused_byte_project_keeps_document_and_history`
- Each regression test covers malformed JSON and a semantic failure after loader writes begin, checking serialized content, undo/redo, dirty state, filename/title and document version.
- Both tests fail with the original implementations restored using `cp`, and pass with the fix restored.
- All 10 `file_pick_tests` pass, including successful disk replacement and preference preservation.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`

Readings: project load/apply implementation, disk and byte open handlers, UI steering, and work-issue skill. Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1613-open-keeps-document.md`.

Base: current upstream/main, as requested; fork main was not changed. Effort: medium. Configured Sonnet worker model unavailable in this session; used session Codex model.

Not exercised: interactive desktop/browser file pickers. `graphify update` unavailable because graphify is not installed.

On the PR-test runner's toolchain, clippy 1.100 flags four indexed loops on main as `needless_range_loop`. That turns `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` red for every PR built there (#1624).

title: fix(project): a typed hole floor no longer reads Stale after save and reopen
body:
## What changed

A Bore op (or Drill, or Thread) whose hole list was edited to a value off the 1 um lattice - the issue's floor typed as `0.190 in - 0.040 in` = `3.8099999999999996` mm - read **Stale** after save and reopen. The file stores the hole as `3.81` (`HoleDto::from_hole` snaps to the lattice), but the stamp taken at generate hashed the unsnapped bits.

- New `crates/app/src/operation/hole_digest.rs`: one hole (and one radial hole) digested with every float snapped by `cl::lattice`, the same snap `HoleDto` / `CrossHoleDto` apply when the file writes the list. The radial `dir` stays verbatim, as the file keeps it. Byte order per hole is unchanged.
- `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`: the Drill (holes + cross), Bore and Thread arms of `stamp_with` call it instead of hashing raw bits (the file shrinks by 28 lines).
- On-lattice holes (everything `detect_holes` emits) hash bit-for-bit as before, so no stamp that matched before changes. A change of half a micron or more still moves the stamp (unit-pinned). No project-file version bump, no posted-output change, no golden or snapshot change.
- Same remedy as #1351 / PR #1352 (`path_sig` hashes moves on the lattice). Snapping at the edit command, the brief's first preference, was dropped: the snap would have to be repeated at every door a hole list comes through (create, edit, paste, GUI table, scripts, old files) and would move the generator's input - the reason #1352 dropped snapping in `Toolpath::new`. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1560-hole-digest-lattice.md`.

## Pins (mutation-checked: `put` hashing raw bits -> all three red; restored -> green)

- `bore_entry::an_edited_hole_floor_off_the_lattice_stays_ok_through_save_and_load` - through the commands: `CreateOperation` Bore, `EditOperationParams` with the off-lattice floor, `GenerateOperation`, `project::save`, `project::load` into a fresh world -> `OpStatus::Ok` (mutant: `Stale`).
- `bore_core::an_edited_hole_floor_off_the_lattice_reopens_ok_and_posts_the_same` - the issue's MCP flow: `detect_holes`, `edit_operation` with `floor_z` 3.8099999999999996 / blind, `generate`, `post` (Fanuc), `save_project`, `open_project` in a new server -> `get_job` status `ok` (mutant: `stale`), and the posted program after reopen is byte-identical to the one before the save.
- `operation::hole_digest::tests::a_typed_floor_stamps_like_the_one_the_file_reloads` - typed and reloaded floors digest alike; 3.81 vs 3.811 still differ.

## Sweep (other DTOs that call `lattice(...)` at save)

- Params: only `HoleDto` and `CrossHoleDto` snap at save - both covered here (Drill holes + radial holes, Bore, Thread). Every other params float is written verbatim (serde's shortest form round-trips the bits, #169).
- Cached-output DTOs (`MoveDto`, `CompSpanDto`, the drill-cycle DTO, `ThreadCycleDto`, the edge-break DTO) store a generated cache, not stamp inputs. The moves feed `path_sig`, already lattice since #1352; nothing else digests the spans, cycles or breaks (grepped every `Hasher` user in `crates/app/src`). No follow-up issue needed.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, sccache): green - wall 10.1 min, 2 steps, 0 failed (it ran every app/ui suite the gate maps name for `app::operation`).
- Named suites, again on their own: app lib (238), project_roundtrip (73), bore_core (5), bore_entry (4), face_holes, operations, mcp, commands_undo, posting, float_roundtrip - 514 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Fork synced at upstream/main c00ba18a.

## Not exercised

- A file already saved before this fix, with a stamp taken from an off-lattice hole, still reads Stale once on reopen; one regenerate stores the new stamp (no re-stamp on load, by design).
- The GUI hole table (it goes through the same `EditOperationParams` and the same stamp).
- Batch and release tiers; Windows.

Changelog: An operation whose hole list was edited to a value off the 1 um grid (e.g. an inch floor) no longer reads Stale after save and reopen (#1560)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1560

title: fix(2d): judge a stock-source cut against the parts in the stock, whatever its kind
body:
Fork synced at v0.19.0. #1615 is merged. This PR is now plain against main. Also fixes #1621 (P1) on the same branch: it touches the same `keep_parts` lines in `run_job`.

A 2D operation whose source is the **stock** (or a pick off it) carried no part law: `part_solid` is false, so `depth_law_of` returned `DepthLaw::None` before the kind's arm. A cut into the part held in that stock had 0 op findings: the program sim held it on an aligned stock, and on a turned stock (the sim refuses to judge) it posted.

## What changed
- `keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind` (new): every 2D kind that carries a part law on a part source - the pocket family (as #1603), Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, Contour, Face, Engrave, Trace. `keep_law::parts_in_stock` now collects the setup's parts (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`: every part, fixtures and a stock-only model left out) for all of them.
- `run_job` (`generate.rs`, both the plain and the 3+2 frame branch): on those parts, Engrave and Trace take the **mark law** (`mark_law::mark_into`, budget `min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)`), every other kind the **solid law** (`contain_into`, nothing excused).
- `mark_law::budget_of`: a stock-source Engrave or Trace declares its mark too, so the program sim credits exactly what the op's law allows (before, the sim judged a stock-source mark against the sharp model: a 0.3 mm mark along the part's outline was refused on an aligned stock).
- A setup with no part judges nothing, as before. Paths are unchanged; only the verdict.

## Readings
#1585 fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block, R15 pocket to Z4, EM-0600-4FL) in a 40 x 40 x 8 box stock over it, aligned and turned 90 deg about Z:

| stock-source case | before: op gouges, aligned / turned | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engrave / Trace Top 8, Bottom 1 (the part's outside wall), Stock or stock top picked | 0, refused by sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular in the pocket 3 mm under its floor | 0, refused by sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Face to Z5 (3 mm into the part's top) | 0, refused by sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Engrave / Trace 0.3 mm along the part's outline | 0, **refused by sim** / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| Contour round the stock to Z1; Slot in the pocket to its floor; Face of a 10 mm stock to Z8 | 0, posts / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| Two parts in one stock, Slot / Trochoidal slot into either part | 0 | yes | refused / refused |

## Pins
`crates/app/tests/stock_source_law.rs` (6; generate, then post; both stocks):
- `engrave_and_trace_off_the_stock_down_the_part_wall_gouge_and_never_post` (Stock and a pick of the stock's top; the mark note named)
- `the_typed_kinds_and_face_off_the_stock_into_the_part_gouge_and_never_post` (Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, Face)
- `a_legal_stock_source_cut_stays_clean_and_posts_on_both_stocks` (Engrave, Trace, Contour, Slot, Face)
- `a_stock_source_cut_with_no_part_in_the_setup_judges_nothing`
- `a_stock_source_cut_answers_for_every_part_in_the_stock` (two parts; a cut into either is convicted)
- `over_mcp_a_stock_source_cut_answers_for_the_part_the_same` (MCP `add_operation` source `stock`, `generate`, `verify`: Engrave, Trace deep and legal; Face into the part)

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | red |
|---|---|
| M1 `parts_in_stock` back to the pocket family only | 11 (the 4 new refusal pins incl. MCP and two-part, and the 7 restated tests) |
| M2 Engrave / Trace judged by the solid law, not the mark law | 4 (legal marks, deep marks, MCP, engrave_law stock pin) |
| M3 sim credit back off for a Stock source | 3 (legal marks post, MCP, sim credit) |
| M4 the mark law not run against the parts | 3 (deep marks, MCP, engrave_law stock pin) |
| M5 only the first part read (`take(1)`) | 1 (two-part) |
| M5b only the last part read | 1 (two-part) |

## Merged with #1615's review fix (4f05e9c0)
#1615 changed `mark_into` to return `Marked` (deep / through / stack) and the note to `mark_law::notes(...)`, and added the material floor (`MARK_FLOOR`, `verify::seat_skin`) and the unlowered shank/holder stack check. Both `run_job` call sites conflicted with this branch's stock-source mark law. Resolution: the mark law picks its mesh as before (the source part on `DepthLaw::Mark`, the setup's parts on a stock-source Engrave / Trace) and passes it to the one `mark_into`, so the floor and the stack check apply to the stock source too; the notes come from `mark_law::notes` in both frame arms. `budget_of` keeps this branch's reading (no `names_part`), `keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind` / `keep_parts` unchanged.
- Pin: `mark_floor.rs::a_stock_source_cut_through_the_plate_meets_the_same_floor` - a Stock-source Engrave / Trace 2.9 mm and 1.9 mm through the 2 mm plate refused by name ("cuts through the part") on both stocks; 0.3 mm posts.

## #1621: a part-source cut answers for the setup's other parts
A part-source op's law read only its source's mesh, so a cut on part B entering part A beside it had no op finding. Measured before (B the #1585 pocket block on x [0,40], A a box on x [-40,-0.7], 80 x 80 x 8 stock): a 0.3 mm Trace / Engrave round B (flank 2.3 mm into A) **posted on both stocks** (the sim credits A the mark budget too); a Contour outside B to Z1 was refused by the sim aligned and **posted turned**.
- `keep_law::neighbour_parts` (new): for a part-source op that carries a part law (`depth_law_of(params, src, true) != None` - Contour, Face, Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, pocket family, Drill without cross, Bore, Thread, Engrave, Trace), the setup's parts (`parts_facets_in`'s set: fixtures and a stock-only model left out) less the entities its source names. Carried on `GenJob::neighbour_parts`.
- `run_job`, both frame arms: those parts take the plain solid law (`contain_into` with `Keep`: nothing excused, no mark budget). The source keeps its own law (Mark budget on the part being marked; Section / Keep / Contain as before).
- Behaviour to know: a whole-model 2D pocket on B in a stock that also holds A clears through A and is now convicted on the op (a real gouge of A).

Pins, `crates/app/tests/neighbour_law.rs` (5; generate, then post; aligned and quarter-turned stock):
- `a_cut_on_b_into_its_neighbour_gouges_on_the_op_and_never_posts` (Trace, Engrave, Contour; gouge on a move that reaches A; turned: refused by the op's moves)
- `a_mark_on_b_within_its_budget_clear_of_a_posts_on_both_stocks` (whole B and B's top picked)
- `a_mark_on_b_deeper_than_its_budget_is_still_judged_by_its_own_law`
- `a_pocket_on_bs_own_floor_is_unchanged_beside_a_neighbour` (same path and findings as with A far away; posts)
- `over_mcp_a_cut_on_b_answers_for_its_neighbour_the_same` (MCP `import_model` x2, `add_operation` source `part`, `generate`, `verify`)
- `area_controls.rs::a_boundary_offset_on_a_tilted_pocket_is_the_flat_offset_pocket_rotated` now also asserts the tower beside the tilted (3+2) pocket is convicted on the op (the neighbour law's frame arm)

## Mutations (each alone, then reverted)
| job | mutation | red |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `seat_skin` emptied (no floor) | `a_stock_source_cut_through_the_plate_meets_the_same_floor` |
| 2 | M1 `neighbour_parts` always empty | into-neighbour pin, MCP pin (2) |
| 2 | M2 the source's own part included (plain solid law on B too) | legal-mark pin, MCP pin (2) |
| 2 | M3 neighbours judged by the mark law with B's budget | into-neighbour pin, MCP pin (2) |
| 2 | M4 a picked source's entities not excluded | legal-mark pin (picked case) (1) |
| 2 | M5 the source's own law stood down when a neighbour exists | deep-mark pin (1) |
| 2 | M7 the neighbour law dropped from the 3+2 frame arm | `area_controls` tilted-pocket test (1) |

The pocket pin is a no-false-positive guard (same path and findings with and without A); none of M1-M5 turns it red, and no plausible mutation found makes it the only one red - recorded honestly.

## Existing tests that changed
Each asserted "a stock source is never judged" on a cut that really enters the part held in the stock:
- `engrave_law.rs`: `a_cut_on_the_stock_is_never_judged_by_the_mark_law` -> `a_cut_on_the_stock_answers_to_the_mark_law_against_the_part`; `the_program_sim_credits_the_mark_and_nothing_past_it` now credits the stock-source 0.3 mm mark (0 cells) and charges a 7 mm one 4.0, like the whole model.
- `trochoid_law.rs`: `a_trochoid_on_the_stock_is_never_judged` (#1593's pin, which #1607 asked to keep or restate) -> `a_trochoid_on_the_stock_answers_for_the_part`.
- `circular_pick_law.rs`: `a_circle_picked_off_the_stock_is_never_judged` -> `..._answers_for_the_part`.
- `circular_entity_law.rs`: `a_stock_source_still_cuts_the_typed_circle_unjudged` -> `a_stock_source_circle_through_the_hole_wall_answers_for_the_part`.
- `slot_picks.rs`: `with_nothing_picked_the_typed_endpoints_rule_as_before` keeps its "cut as typed" assertions; the slot through the pocket walls is now a gouge.
- `posting.rs` `a_gouging_program_is_refused_by_the_verification_gate` and `stock_sim_document.rs` `faced_doc` (20 mm model): a stock-source Face below the part's top was asserted silent; it is now the op's gouge too. The sim's verdict and the refusal text (led by the sim's clause on the aligned stock) are unchanged.

For #1621:
- `area_controls.rs::a_boundary_offset_on_a_tilted_pocket_is_the_flat_offset_pocket_rotated`: the tilted pocket on "part" was compared with a flat one on "twin" in a world that also holds "tower" standing on the block's top; the tilted +3 offset puts the side-on cutter 3 mm into the tower (15 gouges, now on the op), the flat twin has nothing beside it. The frame-door comparison now runs without the tower; the tower's conviction is asserted.
- `stock_source_verdict.rs` (#1094): Op1 (a Bore on the part) now judges the unmarked casting beside it, as the sim does, so its cached verdict carries those gouges; marking the casting raw stock only takes it out of the set, so the three tests that post or read the gate after marking regenerate first (a new `regenerate` helper; `mark` itself unchanged so the undo/redo tests keep their history).

No golden and no snapshot changes.

## Gate
Refresh: main merged in at 4f0bfe7e after #1615 merged (`mark_floor.rs`: both sides kept). `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 4f0bfe7e (app suites 402 s, posting 1 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean on 4f0bfe7e.

Before the refresh: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on c74d888d (sim 99 s, motion 0 s, app 838 s, ui 19 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean on the same tree. (Earlier: green on e6c0f9c0 before the #1615 merge and #1621.)

## Not exercised
- The 3+2 frame branch with a stock-source op over a part (same code shape as #1603's; `tilt.rs` covers only the no-stock case).
- 2D Chamfer and the hole kinds (Drill, Bore, Thread) on a stock source stay at `None` (not in #1607's list; the chamfer's depth is derived and its break is credited only on the part, the hole kinds would need modelled hole rims excused).
- The sim's mark credit still credits a neighbour part the budget (the op is the stricter judge there): #1627.
- The neighbour law tightens by the source's fidelity excess, not each neighbour's.
- **Staleness (#1628, P1, filed):** the op's stamp digests only its source, so a part moved into a stock-source or part-source op's cut AFTER generation leaves the op Ok; on a turned stock that posts (not a regression: before this branch those parts were not judged at all). A stamp term over the kept set was built and pinned here (f4d86b41, 6abccc77) and taken back out (c74d888d): it re-states "workholding never stales", "a stock-based path never reads the model" and the fidelity refusal on a deleted stock source (5 existing tests) - a maintainer's call; #1628 has the options.
- A stock-source Circular legal-path pin: a Circular in the pocket to its floor carries a pre-existing `RapidInStock` on its diagonal exit rapid (present without this change), so the legal row uses the Slot.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1607-stock-source-law.md` (also corrects #1543's and #1593's "a Stock source cuts unjudged"; the #1615 merge and #1621 sections added).

MCP: no new command or tool; `add_operation` / `generate` / `verify` reach the law (pinned).

Changelog: A 2D Engrave, Trace, Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, Contour or Face whose source is the stock (or a pick off it) is judged against the parts standing in that stock - a mark law for Engrave and Trace, the solid law for the rest - so a cut into a part is a blocking gouge on the operation and the post is refused even where the program sim cannot judge; a legal mark off the stock now posts on an aligned stock (#1607). A part-source 2D operation is also judged against the setup's other parts with the plain solid law, so a cut on one part that enters a neighbouring part is refused on the operation (#1621).
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1607
Fixes #1621

title: fix(post): Tormach states the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

**`tormach.cps` states the clearance height before the first X/Y traverse of a section.** This applies after a tool change, after a G30, and at the program start. An upright section first writes `G0 Z<clearance>`:
- The clearance is the stream's `PARAM ClearancePlane`. If the stream does not state it, the post uses the `RetractPlane` (the hop, #1028).
- The clearance is never below the move's own Z.

**A stream that states neither plane is refused by name**, once per program: "first X/Y traverse ... with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) ...".
- **The refused move is not written.** `xyFirst` and `startXY` return false on the refusal. Each caller (rapid, feed, arc, probe guard, probe move, canned cycle) then writes nothing for its move. Every later move with X/Y still unknown is also not written, with no second message. This is the rule from NeoTech's review of #1636 (Fanuc family, #1633). Before the take-over, this PR wrote the combined `G0 X20 Y10 Z2` after the warning.

**Indexed (4th-axis) sections keep their own order.** `indexFor` lifts with G53 and turns A, and their X/Y is the turned tip. In the microARC tester-kit program, the clearance comes immediately after `G0 A0`.

**Why (from a PathPilot Hub run, 770MX sim v2.14.4).** In Hub, T4 was 5" long, and the G54 Z zero was approximately 4.3" below the top of Z travel. After `G43 H4`, the tip was approximately 0.68" below the part top, and the bare `G0 X.. Y..` crossed the part at that height. #1596 lifts again with `G53 G0 Z0` after `G43`. But the top of travel can itself be below the clearance when the tool is long for the work offset. This PR covers that case.
- On a setup that can clear, the new `G0 Z` is a usual move down to the clearance before the traverse.
- On a setup that cannot clear, the control refuses that block because it is past the Z limit, and the program stops. The tool does not rapid through the part.

`assets/posts/AGENTS.md` states the law. `docs/decisions/1614-toolchange-clearance.md` records the decisions and what is taken on trust.

## Take-over by M5 (merge of main)

M5 took this PR over from the user-run session that wrote it. One merge of `upstream/main` (no rebase, no force-push), then one fix commit:
- **`assets/posts/tormach.cps`, the state block (conflict):** this branch added `clearZ` (#1614). Main (#1650) added `afterAsk` and `setupNext` (#1532). Both are kept. No logic conflict: #1650 did not change `xyFirst`, `startXY` or the motion handlers.
- **Four Tormach contour goldens (conflict, from #1577 climb):** main's side taken, then regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` (`conformance`, `program_units`).
- **`crates/app/tests/common/legacy_program.rs`:** merged clean. It is identical on both sides (#1632 and #1636 carried this hunk byte for byte).
- **`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`:** merged clean. #1632 and #1636 did not add a bullet there. The Tormach bullet is kept, and now says that the refused move is not written.
- **`docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.camproj`:** the earlier `WRITE_GOLDEN` run of `microarc_test_part` re-saved it (format v59 to v61, no change to the kit). Main's file is restored. Only the kit `.nc` moves.

## Moved goldens (each differs from main by one added `G0 Z..` line before the first X/Y traverse, nothing else; checked by `git diff -U0 upstream/main`)

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/` (21): `contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `face_square_40x40`, `face_square_40x40_stepped`, `index_4face_microarc4`, `pocket_waterline_plate_with_island`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_bore_centre_mm`, `probe_boss_centre`, `probe_corner`, `probe_edge`, `probe_face`, `probe_guard_moves`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `slot_wide_channel_rows`, `tap_plate`, `trace_plate_with_hole`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/tormach/` (2): `contour_plate_with_hole`, `drill_peck`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_tormach.nc`: `G0 Z5` (ClearancePlane 10 minus OriginZ 5).
- `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/tormach.nc`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/` (6): `arcs`, `drill_retract`, `extreme_coords`, `full_circle`, `full_circle_raw`, `probe`.
- `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc`.

32 files, 32 added lines. No snapshot PNG changed.

### Test inputs that now state the plane that a real section carries
- `tests/common/legacy_program.rs` `as_program` states `PARAM ClearancePlane` from the `START` height of the legacy golden.
- These hand-written streams state `PARAM ClearancePlane`: `tormach_post.rs`, `tormach_program_end.rs`, `tormach_routers.rs`, `tormach_safe_retract.rs`, `tormach_toolchange_lift.rs`, `tormach_fourth_axis.rs`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle.rs`, and `work_offset_index.rs` in the post crate.
- `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up` asserts the new order: a Z-only `G0 Z0.3937` (the 10 mm clearance), then X/Y alone.

## Pinning tests (`crates/post/tests/tormach_traverse_clearance.rs`)

| Test | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z_first` | the `G0 Z` is removed |
| `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated` | the `G0 Z` or the RetractPlane fallback is removed |
| `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height` | the `G0 Z` or the max with the move's own Z is removed |
| `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` | the refusal is removed; the refused move is written (it now asserts no line with an X/Y word, and one message only) |

Mutations: the first four were checked by the author of the PR. After the take-over, the `onRapid` refusal return was removed: the refusal pin failed with `["G0 X20 Y10 Z2", "G0 X20 Y10 Z2"]`. With the return in place, all four pass.

## How tested
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the merged head: post suites ok (24 s); app suites: every suite passes except `lead_approach` (2 tests, `the_reported_keep_down_helix_pocket_enters_every_level_once` and `the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`). These 2 tests also fail on `upstream/main` 389fe96c without this PR (run alone there). That is the known red main, #1675 (after #1656); this PR does not change toolpath generation.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## PathPilot Hub (comment of 03:38Z)
The user ran `drill_peck` from this branch in Hub (770MX sim v2.14.4) before the merge. Every move stayed above the part, and the low traverse is gone. The G30 dip-and-lift that the user saw is the separate issue #1626 (a section that keeps its tool still runs G30). This PR does not change it.

## Not exercised
- A Hub run of the merged head. The motion of the goldens did not change in the merge, except for the main-side changes from #1577.
- The refusal path on a control. No control receives the refused text.
- **Taken on trust:** the `G0 Z<clearance>` is made at the X/Y where the tool change left the spindle. It trusts the stated clearance plane to clear everything under that X/Y (vise, fixture, rotary table). The post cannot know what is there.
- The release-lane `--ignored` suites and the UI suites (no UI code changed).
- Other mill posts: #1632 (grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera) and #1636 (Fanuc family) merged. grblHAL still writes its move after the refusal; that is not in this PR.

Changelog: The Tormach mill post states the section's clearance Z before its first X/Y traverse after a tool change, and refuses (with no motion written) a stream that states no clearance or retract plane, so a tool too long for the work offset stops at the control's Z limit instead of rapiding through the part.

Effort: high (no escalation; taken over by M5).

Fixes #1614

title: fix(2d): judge Engrave/Trace as a mark and keep the part under the pocket family, on the operation itself
body:
Fork synced at v0.19.0; branch merged with upstream/main f2b42e3d (#1597 is in it).

Two P1s with one root: a 2D operation at `DepthLaw::None` had no judge of its own, so its verdict rode on the program sim, and the sim refuses a turned stock. Both are fixed with a law the operation carries. `uncovered()` is unchanged (see below).

## #1595 - Engrave and Trace: the mark law
- `DepthLaw::Mark` (`crates/app/src/operation/mark_law.rs`) for both kinds on a finished-part source, whole model or pick. Under the cutter the part's surface may give way by the **mark budget**, `min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)`, and no more.
- The test is the existing solid law (`verify::solid_hits`) run against the part lowered by the budget. A cutting move that still enters it is a blocking `Warning::Gouge` on that move, and the path carries a note that names the budget.
- It convicts three things: a cut deeper than a mark, a Top typed below the surface, and a wall standing beside the line (a picked pocket floor is traced along the wall's foot).
- The program sim credits the same mark (`stock_sim::credit_marks` in the sim crate, beside #303's `credit_breaks`; the shared walk is now `edge_break::credit_floors`). A column the mark's own cutter swept is judged against `max(that sweep, model top - budget, underside + 0.2 mm)`. The budget is computed from the operation each time, never read from the cached path, and only an Engrave or Trace on the part declares one.
- **A mark is bounded by the part under the cutter** (review fix, 4f05e9c0). The cutting edge may not come within `MARK_FLOOR` (0.2 mm) of an underside of the part: its bottom, or the roof of a void in it. The operation sweeps the edge against the undersides raised into a solid 0.2 mm high (`verify::seat_skin`); the sim adds `underside + MARK_FLOOR` to its credit floor. So a mark is never deeper than `min(budget, thickness under the cutter - 0.2)`. A deeper cut is a blocking `Gouge` and the path note says "cuts through the part".
- **Only the cutting edge gets the budget** (review fix). The shank and holder on a cutting move, and the whole assembly on a rapid, are judged against the part as it stands (`verify::stack_hits`). One excuse: the straight retract up out of the kerf the cutting move before it made (pinned).

Readings on the #1585 fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block, R15 pocket to Z4, 6 mm end mill), whole-model source, Top 8:

| cut | before: aligned / turned | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.02 mm, 0.3 mm deep | refused by the sim / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| 3.0 mm deep (the radius) | refused by the sim / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| 3.1 mm deep | refused by the sim / posts | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| 7 mm deep (the issue's repro) | refused by the sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Top typed 7 (surface at 8), 0.3 stated | refused by the sim / posts | yes | refused / refused |
| pocket floor picked, 0.3 deep | - | yes | refused / refused |

So before this PR no engraving on a model could post on an aligned stock (0.02 mm included), and any depth posted on a turned one.

Readings on the review's thin plate (40 x 40 x 2, 6 mm end mill, whole-model source, Top 2; Engrave and Trace alike):

| cut | op | aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|
| Bottom -0.9 (through the plate; budget 2.9) | Gouge, "cuts through the part" | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| 1.9 mm deep (0.1 mm of plate left) | Gouge, "cuts through the part" | refused (sim charges 0.10) / refused |
| 1.8 mm deep (exactly 0.2 mm left) | 0 | posts / posts |
| 0.3 mm deep | 0 | posts / posts |
| 8 mm block, 2.5 mm deep with 2 mm of flute (shank 0.5 mm in the part) | ShankHit on the part | refused / refused |

At 976cda6c the first row posted on both stocks with no finding (M5's reproduction in pullrequestreview-5900983707).

Re-checked on `Milling-test.step` (EM-0600, whole model, both stocks): Engrave and Trace post at 0.3 mm and at exactly 3.0 mm and are refused at 3.2 mm (the sim charges 0.20 mm); a default whole-model Pocket (stock top to Z10) posts on both stocks. The three changed fixtures are untouched by the review fix.

## #1603 - the pocket family: the keep law
- `DepthLaw::Keep` (`crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`) for 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset on a whole-model source: the solid law alone, against the source's mesh. It applies where the pocket clears the stock around the part (#12). With no stock set up the model is still the volume to remove, and the law stands down (`GenJob::around_part`).
- On a **stock source** (or a pick off the stock) the same law runs against the setup's parts (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`, the mesh the program sim judges against), carried in the job as `keep_parts`. A setup with no part judges nothing.

Readings on the #12 fixture (30 x 30 x 10 block, 12 x 12 boss to Z20, 10 mm end mill, 50 x 50 x 20 stock), cut to Z5:

| case | before: op gouges, turned stock | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| whole model, Area offset +3 (Pocket, Adaptive) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| whole model, extension +5 (Pocket, Adaptive) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| stock source (Pocket, Adaptive; #1554's cut) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| whole model, default controls (Pocket, Adaptive, Offset) | 0, posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| stock source stopping on the part's top | 0, posts | 0 | posts / posts |

## `uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs): not changed
Both issues asked whether a None-law op on a model source should stop counting as judged when the sim cannot judge. It was measured against its own test and declined:
- it would refuse every legal whole-model Pocket, Adaptive and Offset on a turned stock (they were at `None`), which is a false refusal;
- it keeps the verdict tied to whether the sim can model the stock;
- it cannot name the move.

With `Mark` and `Keep`, the only 2D kind still at `None` on a model source is the 2D Chamfer (derived depth, credited by #303). The legal rows above post on a turned stock, pinned.

## Existing tests that changed
Three fixtures ran a stock-source pocket straight through a part and asserted a silent verify. Each is a real cut into the part, which #1603 asks to be refused:
- `post_not_judged.rs`, `machine_switch.rs` (the tilted pocket): the part filled the whole stock. The part is now the 10 mm the pocket leaves, so the cut stops on it. The assertions are unchanged.
- `lead_approach.rs` (two tests on the user's stock-source pocket on `Milling-test.step`): they now assert the gouge on the user's part and read the entry laws on the remaining warnings.
- `authored_law_tests.rs`: #1593's audit table is split into `the_2d_chamfer_alone_stays_unjudged_on_the_part`, `the_pocket_family_keeps_a_whole_model_and_sections_a_pick` and `engrave_and_trace_on_the_part_answer_to_the_mark_law`.

No golden and no snapshot changes. `golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens` pass unchanged.

## Pins
`crates/app/tests/engrave_law.rs` (9; generate, then post, on both stocks; Engrave and Trace):
- `a_whole_model_cut_deep_under_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts_on_either_stock`
- `a_shallow_mark_is_clean_on_the_operation_and_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `the_mark_budget_ends_at_the_cutter_radius_on_both_stocks_alike`
- `a_top_typed_under_the_surface_is_not_a_mark`
- `a_picked_floor_traced_along_its_wall_gouges_the_wall_and_never_posts`
- `a_picked_top_face_marked_shallow_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `a_cut_on_the_stock_is_never_judged_by_the_mark_law`
- `the_program_sim_credits_the_mark_and_nothing_past_it`
- `over_mcp_a_whole_model_engrave_and_trace_are_judged_the_same` (MCP `add_operation`, `verify`)

`crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs` (7; Pocket and Adaptive, both stocks):
- `a_whole_model_area_offset_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_whole_model_extension_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_stock_source_cut_through_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_legal_whole_model_clearing_stays_clean_and_posts_on_both_stocks` (Pocket, Adaptive, Offset)
- `a_stock_source_cut_that_stops_on_the_part_stays_clean_and_posts`
- `a_stock_source_cut_with_no_part_in_the_setup_judges_nothing`
- `over_mcp_the_pocket_family_keeps_the_part_the_same` (MCP `add_operation`, `set_operation_area`, `verify`)

`crates/app/tests/mark_floor.rs` (4, the review fix; generate, then post, on both stocks; Engrave and Trace):
- `a_cut_through_a_thin_plate_gouges_and_never_posts_on_either_stock`
- `a_mark_that_leaves_the_floor_posts_on_both_stocks_and_one_that_does_not_is_refused`
- `the_program_sim_never_credits_a_cut_through_the_plate` (the sim's own verdict, aligned)
- `a_shank_in_the_kerf_is_judged_against_the_part_as_it_stands`

`crates/sim/tests/mark_credit.rs` (9; new: `a_budget_deeper_than_the_plate_never_credits_a_cut_through_it`, `a_mark_on_a_thin_plate_is_credited_down_to_the_floor_it_must_leave`, `a_mark_over_a_void_is_credited_only_down_to_the_roof_it_must_leave`), the unit tests in `mark_law_tests.rs` (13; new: the part under the cutter, a void's roof, the shank, the rapid, the kerf retract, the two notes), `crates/sim/src/verify/seat.rs` (5: undersides whatever the winding, a face between two bodies, a void's roof, the skin, an unreadable mesh) and `authored_law_tests.rs`.

Both fixtures place the box stock centred over the part and assert its bounds.

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | result |
|---|---|
| M1 Engrave / Trace arm back to `None` | red: 6 (deep, radius, low Top, wall, MCP, law table) |
| M2 budget without the radius cap | red: 5 (deep, radius, MCP, sim credit, budget unit) |
| M3 budget without the stated depth | red: 3 (low Top, sim credit, budget unit) |
| M4 part not lowered (the plain solid law) | red: 6 (shallow, picked top, radius, MCP, 2 units) |
| M5 sim mark credit removed | red: 5 (shallow, picked top, radius, MCP, sim credit) |
| M6 sim floor not held to the budget | red: 2 (`mark_credit`, sim credit) |
| M7 sim credits a stock-source cut | red: 1 (sim credit) |
| M8 pocket-family arm back to `None` | red: 4 (offset, extension, MCP, law table) |
| M9 stock-source parts not collected | red: 2 (stock source, MCP) |
| M10 `Keep` with no stock set up | red: 1 (`tilt.rs` parked pocket) |
| M11 `part_solid` early return disabled | red: 5 (stock never judged x2, 3 law tables) |
| M12 lowered part raised 0.05 (over-conviction) | red: 6 (shallow, picked top, radius, MCP, 2 units) |
| **Review fix (run on 4f05e9c0's tree):** | |
| M13 op law: the floor on the underside dropped (no material bound) | red: 4 (`mark_floor` through-cut, floor row; units: part under the cutter, void's roof) |
| M14 sim credit: floor not bound to the underside | red: 4 (`mark_credit` x3: plate through-cut, plate floor, void's roof; `mark_floor` sim verdict) |
| M15 shank, holder and rapids judged against the LOWERED part | red: 4 (`mark_floor` shank in the kerf; units: shank, rapid, kerf retract) |
| M16 `MARK_FLOOR` = 0 (bound by the thickness alone) | red: 8 (`mark_floor` x3, `mark_credit` x2, 3 units) |
| M17 any vertical rapid up excused, not only out of the kerf | red: 1 (unit: kerf retract) |
| M18 a face between two bodies counts as an underside | red: 6 (`seat` unit, 5 `mark_law` units) |
| M19 a through-cut convicted but not named | red: 3 (`mark_floor` x2, notes unit) |

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 4f05e9c0 (sim suites 143 s, motion 4 s, app suites 869 s, ui suites 42 s, 4 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean; `-p camcraft-sim` is clean on the lib, `mark_credit` and `edge_break_credit` (see "Not exercised" for the one lint that is not this PR's). `golden_cl`: 32 passed, unchanged. M1-M12 were run on 086f4010, M13-M19 on 4f05e9c0's tree.

## Not exercised
- The mark and keep laws under a 3+2 frame with a part to keep. The framed branch feeds the local mesh to the same solid law; `tilt.rs` covers only the no-stock stand-down.
- On an aligned stock, when both judges convict, the post's refusal leads with the program sim's clause (the gate's existing order, as in #1597). The op's own gouges are asserted on the op and over MCP.
- The stock-source keep law tightens by the stock's fidelity excess, not each part's.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets` fails locally (rustc 1.100) on `tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs:152` (`needless_range_loop`), which this PR does not touch; the sim lib, `mark_credit` and `edge_break_credit` are clean, and so is `-p camcraft-app --all-targets`.
- The floor under a 3+2 frame: the plane arm feeds the local mesh to the same `mark_into`, so undersides are read along the tool axis; no posed fixture pins it.
- Where the part is thinner than 0.2 mm (a knife edge) the floor stands above the part and convicts an edge passing within 0.2 mm over it; a mesh of several overlapping closed shells is read facet by facet. Both are on the refusing side and are in the decision file.
- NeoTech's two non-blocking notes are not addressed: `budget_of` omitting the `!facets.is_empty()` half of `part_solid_of`, and no test that the sim's and the generate-time budget agree under a 3+2 frame.
- `stock_sim.rs` (app) grew 467 to 477 lines and `generate.rs` by about 60; both were over 400 already. The new code is in new files.

## Follow-ups filed
- #1607 (P1): stock-source Engrave, Trace and the typed kinds cut the part with no op finding and post on a turned stock. Probed here for Engrave and Trace (7 mm, 0 findings, posts). #1603's fix covers the pocket family only.
- #1621 (P1): a part-source 2D cut that enters a NEIGHBOURING part has no op finding (M5's cross-part probe). The fix is the #1607 mechanism (judge against every part of the setup) and #1607 is rewriting those lines on top of this branch, so it is filed to stack there.
- #1608 (P7): `trochoid_law.rs` places its stock beside the part (a box stock is centred on its place), so its aligned rows judge a quarter of it.
- #1554 stays open for its generate-side behaviour (rough the stock minus the part; the skipped narrow band).

MCP: no new command or tool. The existing `add_operation`, `set_operation_area` and `verify` reach both laws (pinned).

Decision: `docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md` (both issues, the `uncovered()` decision, the correction to #1593's audit bullet, which holds only with the default area controls, and the review section: why a fixed 0.2 mm floor, the kerf-retract excuse, and three notes for the maintainer - the budget grows with the cutter, no stock means no keep law, the cross-part gap).

Changelog: An Engrave or Trace on the finished part is judged as a mark (no deeper under the part's surface than the lesser of Top - Bottom and the cutter radius, and never to within 0.2 mm of the part's underside) and a 2D Pocket, Adaptive or Offset keeps the part under an area offset, extension or stock source: a deeper cut is a blocking gouge on the operation and the post is refused even where the program sim cannot judge; a legal engraving on a model now posts (#1595, #1603).
Effort: max (no escalation; #1603 folded in at the coordinator's request)

Fixes #1595

title: fix(post): Tormach lifts Z after each tool change before moving X/Y
body:
## What changed

Every Tormach PathPilot mill tool change posted `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `S.. M3`, then `G0 X.. Y..` with no Z lift between. A bare `G30` leaves Z at the stored G30 height. One stored below the part top (the user's PathPilot Hub sim had machine Z -1.5611, the same cause as #1594) rapids the tool sideways at that height into the part or the vise. M3's review of #1600 raised this to P1.

- `assets/posts/tormach.cps` `startPreamble`: `liftZ()` (`G53 G0 Z0`, or the machine's stated safe Z, #495) right after `G43 H..`. It comes before the spindle start and before the section's first X/Y or A move, including the program's first tool change. The tool-change `G30` stays (PathPilot's convention).
- 4th axis: the new lift comes before `G0 A..`. The index's own lift is kept, so an indexed section has a second, harmless `G53 G0 Z0` just before `G0 A`.
- The issue's other two bare G30s are kept, with the reasons in `docs/decisions/1596-toolchange-lift.md`:
  - **Plasma.** The G30 height is PathPilot plasma's traverse height (rapids carry no Z, and M205 returns to it).
  - **Lathe.** G30 is the X/Z safe spot and there is no "up" to lift to. The lathe's diagonal approach from G30 is a different hazard, filed as #1604 (P3).
- Not stacked: #1600 merged first, and this branch is one commit on current main.

## Pins and mutations

New `crates/app/tests/tormach_toolchange_lift.rs`:

| Pin | Proves |
|---|---|
| `every_tormach_mill_tool_change_lifts_z_before_moving_xy` | Every shipped Tormach mill, both tool changes (the first included): `G43` is followed by `G53 G0 Z0`, the G30 is kept, and there is a lift between each G30 and the next X/Y move. |
| `a_stated_safe_z_is_the_lift_after_the_tool_change` | `safe_retract` 2.0 gives `G53 G0 Z2` after each `G43`. |
| `a_fourth_axis_section_lifts_z_before_the_a_index` | microARC 4: the lift after `G43` comes before `G0 A90`, and A is the first sideways move. |

Mutation check against `tormach.cps`: each mutation was applied, the pins run, and the file restored. All pins were green again after the restore.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove the lift | 3/3 pins red |
| Hard-code the lift to `Z0` | `a_stated_safe_z…` red |
| Move the lift to the end of the preamble (after the spindle and coolant) | 3/3 red |

`tormach_program_end` (#1600) stayed green under every mutation and on the fix: the program end is unchanged.

Updated tests:
- `tormach_safe_retract::a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: the `G53 G0 Z<stated>` count goes from 3 to 5.
- `probe_spindle_stop` (post crate): a `G53` line is a machine-coordinate retract, not the section's first move. The probe `M5` still comes before any work move.

## Goldens

Regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. The tester-kit `.camproj` rewrite that came with it was reverted (unrelated version/float noise).

- 33 `.nc` files changed: 24 app goldens (tormach + inch/tormach + synth_tormach), 8 post goldens (recorded tormach + ream) and the microARC tester-kit `.nc`.
- `git diff -U0 -- '*.nc'` shows exactly **35 added lines, all `G53 G0 Z0`, and 0 removed**: one per tool change.
- No lathe or plasma goldens changed. No snapshot PNGs were touched.

## Gates (macOS, debug)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: ok. The post suites passed (15 s). The app suites passed: the whole app set, since shared goldens changed (800 s).
- Also run: post `recorded_streams` / `script_tormach_plasma`, and app `recorded_post_streams` / `posting` / `lathe_post_tormach` / `tormach_lathes`. All ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No PathPilot Hub or machine run of the new tool change.
- Windows arms of per-OS readings were not run.

Changelog: Tormach mill posts lift Z straight up (`G53 G0 Z<safe>`) after every tool change, before the first X/Y or A move, so a low stored G30 never carries the tool sideways into the part (posted output changes: one line per tool change) (#1596)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1596

title: fix(circular): rings post as arcs, not 512 fixed chords
body:
## What changed

A Circular ring was a closed polygon of 512 chords at every radius, and the helix entry's fallback ramp ("the helix stands down to a ramp along the first cut") walked that polygon back and forth. One Ø6 hole was 74,131 moves of 0.006 mm.

- **Ring cut = two half-turn arcs** about the authored centre at each level (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`, `ring_walk`). G3 for climb, G2 otherwise, starting at the same +X point the polygon started at, so travel direction and climb are unchanged. The ladder walks them through `run_level_walks`, the same `Seg::Arc` walk Bore and Contour use.
- **Polygon sized by tolerance, not 512.** The ring polygon is still used for planning: descent placement, links and the length of the zig-zag ramp. Its chord count is now the fewest power of two from 8 to 512 whose sagitta is within `ARC_FIT_TOL` (0.01 mm), for example 32 for R1. A power of two divides the 512-gon that the cutter-centre disk certificate is built from, so every ring vertex is still a certificate vertex and descents certify exactly as before.
- **The ring ramp flies helical arcs** (`links::push_zig_ring`). It keeps the same out-and-back legs and the same travelled length, so the ramp angle is unchanged. Each leg is at most two half turns, the same pieces `entry::helix_about` already posts. Only Circular opts in (`Motion::with_ring_zig`). Pocket, Bore, Contour and every other ladder keep `push_zig` byte for byte.
- Entry choice, lead, ramp angle, stepdown, stepover, ring-major sequencing and the verify laws are all unchanged.

## Move counts: the issue's table, before and after

Fixture: a 40 x 40 x 10 plate with a modeled Ø6 through hole, `EM-0400-2FL`, the issue's MCP params (seeded Circular plus its patch), whole-model source. The **before** column is upstream main 7bfb1824 on the same fixture and reproduces the issue's numbers exactly.

| Circular params | before | after | arcs after | warnings before -> after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| repro (helix R1, stepover 0.5) | 74,131 | **417** | 364 | 0 -> 0 |
| `entry: plunge` | 13,416 | **156** | 52 | 0 -> 0 |
| `helix_radius: 0.5` | 13,446 | **186** | 108 | 28 -> 28 (the same XY-crossing warnings the issue reports) |
| `stepover: 1.0` | 26,937 | **159** | 132 | 0 -> 0 |
| `stepover: 2.0` | 26,937 | **159** | 132 | 0 -> 0 |
| `radius: 4.0` | 26,858 | **338** | 208 | gouges -> gouges (12,585 -> 345, fewer moves to flag), post still held |
| `radius: 6.0` | 53,690 | **650** | 416 | gouges -> gouges (37,544 -> 811), post still held |
| `stepdown: 2.0` | 67,989 | **345** | 316 | 0 -> 0 |

The radius 4 and 6 rows cut past the modeled Ø6 wall, so they are gouges both before and after. The arcs are judged, not waved through.

## Pins (each mutation-checked)

- `crates/app/tests/circular_arcs.rs::the_issue_table_posts_arcs_and_verifies_the_same`: every row above has a move ceiling (repro <= 500), at least two arcs per ring-level, the same gouge verdict (in-hole rows clean, radius 4 and 6 still gouges).
- `crates/motion/tests/circular_arcs.rs`:
  - `the_issue_hole_posts_a_few_hundred_moves_not_tens_of_thousands`: the repro is under 500 moves with plunge, helix and ramp entries.
  - `each_ring_level_is_two_half_turn_arcs_about_the_centre`: exactly 52 arcs (2 rings x 13 levels x 2). Each has centre = authored centre, endpoints on R1 or R0.5, a diametric half turn, is planar, has `ccw == climb` (both senses tested), and the first one starts at the polygon's old start.
  - `the_ramp_rides_the_ring_as_helical_arcs`: every ramp move is a falling helical arc about the centre on the ring, out and back legs pair up, at most 12 per ring-level.
- `circular.rs` unit test `ring_chords_are_sized_by_the_tolerance`: the sagitta is within `ARC_FIT_TOL`, the count is the fewest power of two that does it, it divides 512, R1 gives 32, and NaN falls back to 512.

Mutations, each red, then restored and green:
- Old `circular.rs` (512 chords, no arcs): all 3 motion pins red. The app pin is red with "74131 moves over 500".
- `with_ring_zig()` dropped (ramp back to chords): the ramp pin and the move-count pin are red.
- First half arc's `ccw` flipped: the direction pin is red.
- `ring_chords` forced to 512: the tolerance unit test is red.
- `ring_chords` compared against 20 x tol: the tolerance unit test is red.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. Motion: lib plus center_cut_law, chamfer_circular, circular_arcs, control_comp, corner_blend, entry_approach, level_links, predrilled_entry, refusal_ghost, tiny_step, wear_comp, xy_arc_entry. App: bore_entry, circular_arcs, control_comp, ladder_entry_height, wear_comp.
- Also green:
  - app: circular_entity_law, circular_pick, circular_pick_law, operations, verify, posting, golden_cl, solid_law_goldens, recorded_post_streams, mill2d_b, units_in_refusals, arc_entry
  - motion: machining2d, entry_arc
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens

**None changed.** No CL or NC golden, recorded post stream or solid-law golden is generated from a Circular op (golden_cl, solid_law_goldens and recorded_post_streams are green with no edits). No snapshot PNGs were touched.

## Breaking?

No. This is a `fix:` that changes the posted output of existing Circular operations: the same circles, depths, direction and entries, in far fewer blocks. Nothing is removed. No parameter, command, project-file field or MCP shape changes. The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1558-circular-arcs.md`.

## Not exercised

- No real post into a controller or the Hub sim. The arcs are the same `Move::arc` shape the helix entry already posts, and `posting` is green.
- No release-lane heavy suites and no Windows run.
- The vault mode uses the same ring walk. It is covered by `chamfer_circular` and `mill2d_b` (green), with no new vault-specific pin.
- Posts without helical-arc support: the helix entry already emits helical arcs on every post, and this adds no capability gate.

Changelog: Circular posts each ring as two arcs (G2/G3) and its ramp entry as helical arcs on the ring, instead of 512 fixed chords per ring: a Ø6 hole drops from 74,131 moves to 417 (#1558)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at upstream main 7bfb1824.

Fixes #1558

title: fix(post): Tormach programs end at the top of Z - no trailing G30
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` (the Tormach PathPilot mill post) now ends every program at the top of Z:

```
M9          (only when coolant ran)
M5
G53 G0 Z0   (or the machine's stated safe Z, #495)
G20/G21     (only when the EndUnits option asks, #596)
M30
```

The `G30` that followed the final retract is gone, and no `G0 A0` is added. The `G30` before each tool change (`G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `T.. M6`) is unchanged. The end retract and the tool-change retract are split: `liftZ()` is the `G53 G0 Z` lift both use, and `retract()` (tool change only) adds the G30. The footer comment is rewritten to the new behaviour and cites #1594 and the user's Hub result.

## Evidence (from the issue)

The user ran four hand-written endings in PathPilot Hub (770MX sim, v2.14.4, 2026-11-13), with the sim's stored G30 low (machine Z -1.5611):

| Ending | Result |
|---|---|
| A: `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30` (the old post) | goes up, then G30 drives the tool down below the part top |
| B: `G30` only | drives the tool down from Z+0.5 to the G30 Z |
| C: `G53 G0 Z0` only | ends at the top of travel and stays there |
| D: `G53 G0 Z0`, `G0 A0` | not wanted |

The user chose C ("C is the only right one"). This PR posts C.

## Fix, not breaking

The posted output changes only in its last lines, and the change corrects wrong behaviour a user hit (P3 bug), so it is `fix(post)`. No project-file field, parameter or command changes. The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1594-tormach-end-g53.md`.

## Pins

New `crates/app/tests/tormach_program_end.rs`:
- `every_tormach_mill_program_ends_z_up_then_m30_with_no_g30`: every shipped Tormach mill machine ends `M5`, `G53 G0 Z0`, `M30`, with nothing after the final G53 but M30. Both tool changes still read `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `T.. M6`.
- `a_stated_safe_z_ends_at_that_z_with_no_g30`: a Tormach file stating `safe_retract` 2.0 in ends `G53 G0 Z2`, `M30`, with no G30 anywhere.
- `a_fourth_axis_program_ends_without_returning_a`: a job indexed to A90 on the 770MX + microARC 4 ends with nothing after the final G53 but M30 (no `G0 A`, no G30).

Updated to the new ending: `tormach_post::a_pathpilot_program_has_no_fence_and_no_o_or_n_words`, `tormach_safe_retract` (three tests: 2 tool-change G30s plus a G30-free end), `tormach_end_units` (the G20/G21 goes between `G53 G0 Z0` and `M30`).

**Mutation checks** (all restored to green afterwards):
- Put the G30 back at the end (`onClose` calls `retract()` again): `every_tormach_mill_...` and `a_fourth_axis_...` go red. So do `tormach_post::a_pathpilot_program_...`, both `tormach_end_units` G20/G21 tests, and two `tormach_safe_retract` tests. `a_stated_safe_z_...` stays green, which is correct: a machine with a stated non-zero safe Z never got the G30 (its behaviour is unchanged and pinned).
- Add `G0 A0` after the end lift: all three new pins go red.
- Drop the tool-change G30 from `retract()`: `every_tormach_mill_...` goes red.

## Goldens

33 Tormach mill NC goldens changed, and every changed line is the same removed `G30` right before `M30` (`git diff upstream/main -- '*.nc'` shows 33 `-G30` lines and no other `+`/`-` lines). The files:
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/*` (21, including `index_4face_microarc4`), `inch/tormach/*` (2), `synth_tormach.nc`
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/*` (7), `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/tormach.nc`
- `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc`

The kit README's steps 1 and 7 now describe the new end. No snapshot PNGs are touched. The lathe and plasma goldens are unchanged.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 0 failed. The shared golden inputs changed, so the gate ran the full post suites (28 s) and app suites (812 s), 3337 tests passed. That covers `recorded_post_streams`, `posting`, `recorded_streams`, `script_tormach`, `tormach_post`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `tormach_end_units`, `tormach_safe_retract`, `tormach_program_end`, `microarc_test_part` and the inch NC goldens.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app` on the touched test targets with `-D warnings`: clean.
- macOS. Branched from upstream/main 7bfb1824 (newest cut tag v0.19.0); the fork's own main is not synced to that tag.

## Not exercised

- No PathPilot Hub or machine run of a CamCraft-posted program with this ending. The reference is the user's hand-written program C.
- No Windows run.

## Follow-up

#1596 (P7): `tormach-plasma.cps` and `tormach-lathe.cps` also end with a bare `G30`, and the mill's tool-change `G30` carries the same low-G30 risk. Both were out of this issue's scope, which covered the mill program end.

Changelog: Tormach PathPilot mill programs now end with `G53 G0 Z0` then `M30`. The trailing `G30` is gone, so a low stored G30 position can no longer drive the tool back down at the end of the program.

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #1594

title: feat(2d): trochoidal method for 2D Adaptive, confined to its region
body:
## What changed

2D Adaptive gets a **Method** choice (maintainer's decision of 2026-11-13, "Adaptive op only"):

- **Spiral** (default): the HSM plan the kind always ran. Same bytes, same stamp; no existing golden moved.
- **Trochoidal**: trochoid loops inside the operation's region (its selection and boundary settings).

This is the 2D Adaptive slice of #1509. 2D Pocket is not touched (#1517). 3D Adaptive and the rest are filed as sub-issues (below).

### The trochoidal method (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch.rs`)

- The cutter-centre area is the region eroded by the tool radius plus the stock to leave (the pocket's own law).
- The lane is that area's medial line (`adaptive::medial`), straightened. The loop band is the least clearance along it, so every cutter-centre point is inside the area by construction.
- The loops, the measured-engagement step ladder and the lifted returns are the Trochoidal slot's planner (`trochoid_slot`, #220). The forward step is at most optimal load x D; the limit is 90 degrees of contact, measured on the dexel stock.
- The finished path is then checked move by move against the area (`confined`). A point outside refuses the whole operation by name, with its place and a ghost.
- A band wider than the tool gets an opened bore (`trochoid_bore.rs`): helix at half the tool radius, then a two-centre semicircle spiral out to the band. A helix of the band's radius leaves a post at the lane's start when the band is wider than the tool. The stand-alone slot keeps its plain bore byte for byte (its own post is #1589).

Sources: Otkur & Lazoglu 2007 and Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009 (trochoidal milling); Blum 1967 and Held 1991 (medial line); Douglas & Peucker 1973 (straightening). No vendor material.

### Refused by name

| Case | Refusal |
|---|---|
| Empty region | `nothing to machine: empty pocket region` |
| Region narrower than the tool | `the region is narrower than the 6.000 mm tool ...` |
| Too narrow to loop in | `the region is <w> mm wide where the loops would run, too narrow for a 6.000 mm tool to loop in (it needs more than 6.260 mm)` |
| Ring round an island | `the region closes round an island ... use the Spiral method` |
| No single medial line (L, T, island pocket) | `the area is no single channel ... use the Spiral method` |
| One lane would leave over 25 % out of reach | `loops along its medial line would leave <n> % of the region standing (at most 25 %)` |
| A loop outside the region | `a loop at (x, y) would leave the region - nothing is cut` |
| Drop past the helix turn cap | `the bore helix would need more than <cap> turns ... (half the tool radius)` |
| Zero / oversized optimal load, zero stepdown | the Adaptive doors (`PocketParams::validate`) |

Under 25 % the unreached area (the corners of a rectangular pocket) is said in the notes in mm2 and per cent.

### Laws

- **Everything is a command**: the Method is an `EditOperationParams` edit (undo / redo tested).
- **MCP**: `edit_operation` / `add_operation` take `"method": "spiral" | "trochoidal"` through the parameter DTO; an unknown word is refused. No new tool was needed.
- **Project file**: `adaptive2_d.method`; absent (every older file) reads as `spiral`. Additive, the format version does not move.
- **Stamp**: the method byte is written only for Trochoidal, so every Spiral operation keeps its stamp.
- **UI**: a Method combo on the Passes tab of 2D Adaptive (not on 2D Offset); structural test only, no snapshot PNG.
- **Decisions**: `docs/decisions/1509-adaptive-trochoid-method.md`. The stand-alone Trochoidal slot operation is kept as the confined slot #1503 made it; nothing is migrated (#1590 asks the maintainer to confirm).
- **Code shape**: new files 32 to 278 lines; `trochoid_slot.rs` went from 405 to 388 lines (its bore moved to `trochoid_bore.rs`); `mill2d_page.rs` stays at 400. No new crate dependency. No `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!` outside tests.

## Readings

34 x 16 pocket face, 6 mm end mill, default optimal load (14.6 % of D), two levels:

- 20 loops of radius 5.039 mm a level at a 0.859 mm step; 86.0 degrees measured (limit 90.0).
- No slotting; no feed crosses another (`crossed_pairs`).
- Cutter centre within 0.002 mm of the eroded face.
- 49.7 mm2 (9 %) of the region out of the loops' reach (its corners), said in the notes.
- App level, through the commands: no warning blocks the post, `verification_report` has no problem (the stock sim finds no gouge), Fanuc post writes.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch_tests.rs` (12 tests): inside the region and under the limit; the opened bore leaves no post (and the plain bore does); each refusal by name; retract returns without lift room.
- `crates/app/tests/adaptive_trochoid.rs` (5 tests): picked pocket face generates, verifies, posts and matches `tests/golden/adaptive2d_trochoidal_pocket_face.cl`; stamp; too-narrow face refused and nothing posts; undo / redo; older file reads as Spiral; MCP sets the method, refuses an unknown word, generates and verifies.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/adaptive_method.rs` (2 tests): the Method row and its combo value; none on 2D Offset.

Mutation check (each line deleted or neutralised, its test run, then restored): 10 of 10 killed.

| Mutation | Killed by |
|---|---|
| empty-region refusal removed | `an_empty_region_is_nothing_to_machine` |
| narrower-than-tool refusal removed | `a_region_narrower_than_the_tool_is_refused_by_name` |
| too-narrow-to-loop refusal removed | `a_region_too_narrow_to_loop_in_is_refused_by_name_with_the_numbers` |
| ring refusal replaced by "use the closed line" | `a_ring_round_an_island_is_refused_by_name` |
| rest limit 25 % raised out of reach | `a_lane_that_would_leave_most_of_the_region_standing_is_refused_by_name` |
| `validate()` call removed | `a_zero_or_oversized_load_is_refused_by_name_never_looped_forever` |
| path check `confined` neutralised | `a_loop_outside_the_region_is_refused_by_the_check_on_the_path` |
| opened bore switched off | `the_opened_bore_leaves_no_post_at_the_lane_start` |
| stamp byte for Trochoidal removed | `the_trochoidal_method_stays_in_the_picked_face_posts_clean_and_matches_its_golden` |
| `#[serde(default)]` on `method` removed | `a_new_2d_adaptive_is_spiral_and_an_older_file_reads_as_spiral` |

The first version of the stamp test (status goes Stale after an edit) survived its mutation: an edit makes the operation Stale whatever the digest says. The test now compares `current_stamp` for the two methods directly.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 9b79a44b - green, 3 steps, 0 failed (motion suites 417 s, app suites 1929 s, ui suites 55 s; 40.1 min wall). Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion, camcraft-app and camcraft-ui, all targets: clean.

## Not exercised

- No NC (G-code) golden for the new method: the test asserts the post writes, the CL is pinned.
- No GUI run by hand and no machine run. The Method combo is asserted structurally only.
- Curved channels: the lane follows a bent medial line through the slot planner's chain layout, and the path check and the crossing law judge the result, but no test pins a curved region.
- Release-mode heavy lanes were not run (quick tier only).
- The existing `trochoid_slot_small.cl` golden (band narrower than the tool) proves the stand-alone slot's output did not move for that case; a stand-alone slot with a band wider than the tool has no golden, its bore code path is unchanged (`open: false`).

## Sub-issues filed (Part of #1509)

- #1587 - trochoidal method for wide and branching regions (parallel lanes, islands, corner clean-up); P4, effort:max
- #1588 - engagement limit, return and loop width as page and MCP parameters; P7, effort:high
- #1590 - decide the stand-alone Trochoidal slot operation's future; P8
- #1591 - 3D Adaptive: Method choice with a Trochoidal method per level; P4, effort:max
- #1589 - bug found on the way: the stand-alone Trochoidal slot leaves a post at its start when its loop band is wider than the tool; P3

Changelog: 2D Adaptive has a Method choice - Spiral (default, unchanged) or Trochoidal, which clears a channel-like region with loops along its medial line, confined to the region and refused by name where one lane cannot cut it

Effort: max (not escalated)

Refs #1509

title: fix(2d): judge a Trochoidal slot against the finished part like the Slot
body:
Fork synced at v0.19.0; branched from upstream/main 7bfb1824 (after #1585 merged).

## What changed
- `depth_law_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`): `OpParams::TrochoidalSlot` joins the Slot and Circular arm, `Slot | TrochoidalSlot | Circular => authored_law(src)`, still after the `part_solid` early return. An Entity or Selection source naming the finished part is `DepthLaw::Section`; a Stock source (or a pick off the setup's stock) still cuts unjudged.
- #1513's `slot_fit::refuse_unfit_slot` is unchanged. A picked slot that does not fit its region in XY is still refused at generate. The new law adds the depth check, and on a whole model the walls, which the fit check never read.
- **Root cause:** TrochoidalSlot fell to `_ => DepthLaw::None`, so nothing on the operation judged its hand-typed endpoints and width. `uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs) counts any fresh, stamped op as judged, so the post relied on the program sim alone. The sim refuses to judge a turned stock, and it missed the through-wall case even with the stock aligned.
- Doc comments, `authored_law_tests.rs` and `docs/decisions/1593-trochoid-law.md` (decision plus an audit of the other kinds) are updated.

## Other 2D kinds still at `None` on a part-solid source (audit)
Probed on the same fixture, with a whole-model source cut to Z1:
- **Pocket / Adaptive2D / Offset2D, whole model:** left as is. By contract the source is the volume to remove. Every move below the floor stays outside the part (radius 23+ against the 20 mm half-block), and the program sim agrees. Picks were already `Section`.
- **Chamfer2D:** left as is. It enters the part by design, and its depth is derived, not typed.
- **Engrave / Trace:** left at `None` (Section would convict legal engravings). They are **filed as P1 #1595**: cut to Z1 on a whole model, they run 3-7 mm under the model. The aligned program sim refuses that, and with the stock turned it posts.
- **Drill with cross holes:** this is the lathe turret's cross drill, judged by its own laws, not a 2D mill kind.

This table is pinned by `the_kinds_that_enter_or_remove_the_part_by_contract_stay_unjudged`.

## Pins (`crates/app/tests/trochoid_law.rs`, fixture: 40x40x8 block, R15 pocket to Z4, 6 mm EM; all go through generate, then verify, then post)
- `a_whole_model_trochoid_through_the_pocket_wall_gouges_and_never_posts`: x 4..20, 10 wide, at the floor. With the stock aligned **and** turned, the op has gouges and `post_setup` refuses with "T1: move N cuts past the finish surface". No file is written.
- `a_whole_model_trochoid_under_the_floor_gouges_and_never_posts_where_the_sim_cannot_judge`: 3 mm under the floor. With the stock turned, the post is refused on the op's own gouge. With it aligned, the op gouges and the post is refused (the sim's clause leads the message).
- `a_picked_trochoid_that_fits_its_floor_but_sinks_under_it_never_posts`: a floor pick that fits in XY, 3 mm deep, stock turned. The post is refused on the op's gouge.
- `a_trochoid_inside_the_pocket_at_its_floor_stays_clean_and_posts`: no blocking finding on either stock, and it posts on the aligned one.
- `a_trochoid_on_the_stock_is_never_judged`: a `SrcRef::Stock` source and a pick on the from-model stock's floor both get 0 gouges.
- `over_mcp_the_whole_model_trochoid_is_judged_the_same`: `add_operation` "Trochoidal slot" with source "part", then `verify`. The wall case gives op gouges with `ok:false`; the legal case gives `ok:true`.
- Unit tests: `the_trochoidal_slot_answers_to_the_same_authored_law`, the audit table above, and TrochoidalSlot added to `a_source_that_is_not_the_part_is_never_judged`.

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | trochoid_law result |
|---|---|
| M1 TrochoidalSlot arm removed (back to `None`, the pre-fix code) | red: wall, under-floor, picked, MCP (4) |
| M2 `authored_law` Entity -> None | red: wall, under-floor, MCP (3) |
| M3 `authored_law` Selection -> None | red: picked (1) |
| M4 `part_solid` early return disabled | red: stock never judged (1) |
| M5 verify `gouge_tol` -> -0.05 (over-conviction) | red: legal stays clean, MCP legal, stock (3) |
| tightening `contain_into`'s allowance | survives; that is the Contain kinds' law, never reached by Section, so it is equivalent here |

Goldens unchanged: golden_cl 32 passed, solid_law_goldens passed. trochoid_confine (#1503/#1513) and trochoid_op pass.

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 5482f653 (app suites 716 s, ui suites 47 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
A tilted-frame (`Some(frame)`) Trochoidal slot on a part source has no dedicated pin; the framed branch feeds the local model to `Section` the same way it does for the Circular.

Changelog: A Trochoidal slot on the finished part (whole model or pick) is now judged against it: a channel typed through a wall or below the floor is a blocking gouge on the operation and the post is refused, even where the program sim cannot judge (#1593).
Effort: high (no escalation)
