title: fix(setup): refuse generation under a WCS tilted off the machine Z
body:
## What changed

A milling setup's WCS can be turned onto another face from the WCS pane, but every milling generator cuts along the machine's Z. The turned WCS was drawn and then ignored: the reporter's Setup2 facing machined the face that is level in the model (the wrong face) and the op said "OK". The post already refused any rotated work offset (#315), so no wrong G-code could post. The toolpath was still wrong, though, and nothing on screen said so.

- New `crates/app/src/setup_wcs_tilt.rs`: `generation_problem` / `setup_problem` return a named refusal when a milling setup's WCS Z is tilted off the machine's +Z (more than 1e-9 rad, the post's identity tolerance).
- `collect_job` (the generation door) refuses with it: *"setup 'Setup2': its WCS (G54) has its Z axis tilted 90.000 deg off the machine's Z - the tool always cuts along the machine's Z, so this would machine the part as it lies, not as the WCS shows; turn the part with the setup's Part alignment instead and keep the WCS Z pointing up"*.
- A facing pick on a face that is level only in the tilted WCS (the reporter's first error) now names the WCS as the reason instead of suggesting a 2D Contour. It keeps the "is not horizontal - a facing pass needs a floor" door phrase, so `door_refusal` still treats it as a door refusal.
- A WCS turned only about Z (a squared-up offset) still generates. Its post refusal is #315's, unchanged.
- Milling only (`Kind::Mill`). Lathe, wire and the other machine kinds are not affected.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1510-tilted-wcs.md`. Actually generating in the WCS frame was considered and dropped: that is effort:max work, and Part alignment (#326) already turns the part for a setup.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_tilt.rs::a_tilted_setup_wcs_refuses_generation_by_name`: the reporter's case (Setup1 square, Setup2 WCS turned 90 deg about X). Setup2's face is refused by name and Setup1's still generates.
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_tilt.rs::a_wcs_turned_only_about_z_still_generates`: the scope guard (yaw only still generates).
- `crates/app/tests/pick_doors.rs::a_wall_level_only_in_a_tilted_wcs_names_the_wcs`: the pick refusal names the tilted WCS and Part alignment.

Mutation check (standing rule):
- Deleted the `setup_wcs_tilt::generation_problem` check in `collect_job`: `a_tilted_setup_wcs_refuses_generation_by_name` went RED. Restored: GREEN.
- Deleted the tilted-WCS branch in `selection.rs`: `a_wall_level_only_in_a_tilted_wcs_names_the_wcs` went RED. Restored: GREEN.

Also run by hand, all green: rotated_wcs, commands_undo, mcp_model, mcp_setup, mcp_wcs_features, one_wcs, project_roundtrip, rotary_verify, wcs_align, wcs_roles, posting, setup_sheet, setups, heights, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, wcs_view_pose, circle_centre, face_origin, operations, setup_align.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`. green: 1 step (19 app suites + app lib), 0 failed, 4.3 min wall; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The GUI by hand. The refusal reaches the op status and status line the way every `GenError::Invalid` does, and no UI code changed, so there are no structural assertions or snapshots to update.
- Ops in a non-mill setup under a tilted WCS. They are out of scope on purpose.

Changelog: A milling setup whose WCS Z is tilted off the machine's Z is now refused at generation by name (pointing at Part alignment), instead of quietly facing the wrong face; a facing pick that is level only in the tilted WCS says why (#1510)

Effort: high (no escalation)

fork synced at v0.19.0 (branch merged with upstream/main for the PR; conflicts were only the fork's process-sync files, upstream's taken)

Fixes #1510

title: fix(trochoid): a Trochoidal slot stays inside its selection or is refused; the post judges it for gouges
body:
## What changed

A Trochoidal slot with a selection picked (a face or edge chains) generated a path across the selected pocket's wall into the model and reported **OK** (#1503, maintainer screenshot). Generation now refuses such a slot by name, with the numbers:

> Trochoidal slot: the 16.000 mm wide slot from A (-20.000, 0.000) to B (20.000, 0.000) does not fit its selection - it needs 8.000 mm clear each side of its centre line, but the selection's edge comes within 5.000 mm at (...), so the cut would run 3.000 mm past the selection into the model; shorten or narrow the slot, or select the region it should cut

- New `crates/app/src/operation/slot_fit.rs`: `refuse_unfit_slot(kind, a, b, width, region)`. This is pure plane geometry. The slot's capsule (centre line A-B, half-width width/2) must lie inside the picked region: both endpoints inside, and every boundary edge of every loop (holes included) at least width/2 from the centre line, with 1e-4 mm of slack so a slot exactly as wide as its pocket still fits. The generator already keeps every loop inside that band (`contained` in motion `trochoid_slot`), so the check covers what is cut. It refuses rather than clips, which is simpler and safe.
- `operation/generate.rs`: the TrochoidalSlot arm resolves its region first. When the source is a selection, it calls the helper before generating.
- No selection: nothing changes. The typed endpoints rule, and the post judges the path against the model.

**Step 0 (posted on #1503):** on upstream main df90b031 the post **already refused** this slot through the stock-sim gouge clause: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 5926 cell(s), worst 20.00 mm at (-25.31, -5.94, z 0.00)`. The gap was at generation, where the status was `ok` with cached blocking `Gouge` findings. Nothing opts this op out of the gouge check. The page text "Boundary settings do not apply" only means the area controls (offset, extension) are not used.

**Shared with #1504:** the helper takes the kind's label, so the plain Slot can call it unchanged. Slot is excluded in `selection_drives_region`, so its arm sees the authored stadium today, not the picks; #1504 (M3) owns that. Noted on #1503 and #1504. The Slot arm is not touched here.

**Split:** Expected item 2 (trochoidal motion as a 2D Adaptive method) is out of this PR. It is filed as #1509 (Part of #1503, effort:max). That is why this PR says `Refs #1503`, not Fixes: #1503's Done means includes the Adaptive method. The maintainer can close #1503 when this merges if #1509 carries item 2.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/trochoid_confine.rs`. The fixture is an 80 x 60 x 20 block with a 50 x 25 pocket to z 10 (floor face 1250 mm2, as in the screenshot) and a 6 mm `EM-0600-4FL`.

| Pin | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `a_slot_longer_than_its_selected_pocket_face_is_refused_by_name` | The screenshot setup (A (-20,0), B (20,0), width 16, floor face picked) is refused by name with 8.000 / 5.000 / 3.000. No path is cached and nothing posts. |
| `mcp_refuses_the_same_slot_by_name` | The same refusal over MCP: `add_operation` (seeded A/B/width), `set_operation_geometry` (floor face), `generate`. The post is refused too. |
| `a_slot_that_fits_its_selection_generates_and_posts_clean` | A (-12,0) to B (12,0), width 16 generates with no blocking warning. The program gate (stock sim against the model) is empty and it posts. No false refusal. |
| `the_post_refuses_an_unconfined_trochoid_that_enters_the_model` | With no selection, the same slot through the end walls generates, and the post's stock-sim gouge clause refuses it (`gouge: program cuts below the model ...`). |
| `slot_fit::tests` (unit, 2) | Fits, exactly-as-wide fits, past the end wall refused with numbers, endpoint outside, centre line across a hole. |

Mutation checks (revert the guard, confirm red, restore, confirm green):
- Confinement call disabled (`if false && ...` in generate.rs): `a_slot_longer...` and `mcp_refuses...` are **red**, the other two green. Restored: 4/4 green.
- Sim gouge clause blinded (`Ok(sim) if false && sim.dev.gouge_cells > 0` in posting_sim.rs): `the_post_refuses...` is **red**, the others green. Restored: 4/4 green.
- Guard made 5 mm too strict (`d + FIT_TOL < half + 5.0`): `a_slot_that_fits...` is **red** (a false refusal is caught). Restored: 4/4 green.

Gates (local, macOS, fork synced at upstream main df90b031): the quick gate's app step (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, 167 app suites incl. trochoid_op, trochoid_confine, operations, posting, mcp, mcp_order, stock_sim_document, slot_caps, pocket_overhead, plus mcp_verify, mcp_pick, mcp_pockets, pocket_recognition) all green, and `camcraft-app --lib` 186/186 after a fix to my own unit fixture. motion `trochoid_slot` green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. The quick gate's ui step (boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, feedback, machine, operations, sinker_setup) was **not run**: no ui code changed, and those suites open windows.

## Not exercised

- The UI page text ("Boundary settings do not apply to it") is unchanged. The structural UI test is not touched, and the ui suites were not run (no ui code changed; they open windows).
- Depth: a slot whose bottom is below the picked floor face is not refused at generation. The verify pass caches blocking `Gouge` findings and the post's sim refuses it, as for every other op.
- Edge-chain selections go through the same picked region. Only the face pick is pinned.

Changelog: A Trochoidal slot with a selection is refused by name, with the numbers, when its endpoints and width do not fit inside the selected region, instead of generating across a wall into the model (#1503)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #1503

title: feat(pocket): pre-drilled entry - plunge down proved drilled holes (#1449, slice 1)
body:
First slice of #1449: a 2D Pocket can enter each level by a straight plunge down a hole that a Drill operation ahead of it in the same setup made. It does this only where that hole is proved open. Everything else keeps the asked helix, ramp or arc, and the path says why by name.

Branched from upstream/main at ba3776b1 (the mkinney fork's main is on v0.18.0; this branch carries upstream's current process files).

## What changed

- **`camcraft-motion`**
  - New `Approach::predrilled` flag (default off).
  - New `machining2d::predrilled` module and `pocket_entered(region, params, holes)`; `pocket()` is unchanged and calls it with no holes.
  - The ladder's `descent::plan` takes a proved hole ahead of every arm. A hole is used only when it is open to the level's Z, its centre is a legal cutter centre, and the dive link from it to the pass start is proved. When no hole serves a level, the asked entry stands and a note says why.
  - The pass plan is re-seated on the deepest proved hole: a ring is rotated, an open zigzag pass is split into a forward tail and a reversed head. The link from the hole is then the shortest one to any pass, so it crosses none (verify's Crossing law stays silent).
- **`camcraft-app`**
  - New `operation::predrilled_entry::proved_holes`. Hole centres come from the moves of the Drill ops ahead (`rest::drills_ahead`, now also collected for a Pocket with the flag on). A hole is kept only if:
    - the drill's stated diameter is at least the tool's + 2 x 0.1 mm clearance;
    - the prior grid (the stock the program ahead leaves, as the drilling and thread laws read it) holds no material over the tool disc + clearance above the counted depth;
    - the counted depth is the deeper of the grid reading and the drill point's cone at the disc radius.
  - Unprovable cases are named and the hole is left out: no drill, a drill too narrow (with the numbers), an unreadable prior, a posed 3+2 pocket.
  - File: `links.approach.predrilled` (written only when on). Stamp: byte `0xC7` only when on. The pocket already goes Stale when the program ahead changes.
  - Door: the flag on any kind other than 2D Pocket is refused by name (`PREDRILLED_POCKET_ONLY`), never silently dropped.
- **Command / MCP:** the flag is an ordinary params field, so `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and MCP `edit_operation` / `add_operation` set it with `{"links": {"approach": {"predrilled": true}}}`. No new command or tool was needed.
- **Decision:** `docs/decisions/1449-predrilled-entry.md`.

## How tested (pins, each mutation-checked)

| Pin | Test(s) | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hole proved: plunge at every level, no helix; posted G-code has `G00 X0 Y0 Z..` then `G01 X0 Y0 Z12 F200`; verify silent; posts through the gate | app `a_drilled_hole_ahead_is_plunged_to_full_depth_and_posted`, motion `a_proved_hole_is_plunged_at_every_level_with_no_helix` | entry never plunges | caught |
| Delete the drill: the pocket goes Stale at once; regenerated, it has no plunge and uses the helix | app `deleting_the_drill_takes_the_plunge_away`, `without_the_drill_the_helix_stands_and_says_why` | pocket stamp ignores the program ahead | caught |
| Hole the grid does not show is never air | unit `a_hole_the_grid_does_not_show_is_never_air`, `an_unreadable_prior_proves_nothing` | floor from drill moves only, grid dropped | caught |
| Drill narrower than tool + clearance (Ø4 into Ø4, 4.2 needed): left out by name | app `a_drill_no_wider_than_the_tool_plus_clearance_is_refused_by_name`, unit twin | width check dropped | caught |
| Shallow hole: only the levels it reaches plunge; the floor level helixes, named with the Z numbers | app + motion `a_shallow_hole_serves_only_the_levels_it_reaches` | depth check dropped | caught |
| Hole outside the cutter-centre area is never plunged | motion `a_hole_outside_the_cutter_area_is_never_plunged` | area AND link proof dropped together | caught |
| Area check alone (`predrilled.rs` entry filter) | unit `predrilled::tests::a_hole_outside_the_cutter_area_is_refused_even_at_the_pass_start` | area check dropped | caught (only this pin) |
| Link proof alone | unit `predrilled::tests::a_hole_whose_link_crosses_a_planned_pass_is_refused` | link proof dropped | caught (only this pin) |
| Non-centre-cutting tool keeps its entry, named | motion `a_tool_that_is_not_centre_cutting_keeps_the_asked_entry` | guard dropped | caught |
| Undo/redo, file round trip, refused on another kind; MCP set + undo + refusal on adaptive | app `the_flag_is_an_undoable_edit_and_refused_off_the_pocket`, `mcp_sets_and_undoes_the_flag` | - | - |

Also: `with_the_flag_off_the_drill_is_never_read`, `without_a_hole_or_the_flag_the_helix_stands`, `a_non_finite_hole_is_ignored`, `a_posed_pocket_and_no_drill_are_named`, `an_open_wide_hole_is_handed_over_to_its_cone_depth`.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, head 9d098fe8): green - motion suites 140 s, app suites 691 s, ui suites 18 s, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean (without `--no-deps` the newer clippy flags three pre-existing `needless_range_loop` sites in the untouched `camcraft-geometry` feature.rs).

## Not exercised / remaining on #1449

- UI: no "Entry positions (pre-drilled)" group yet, so no structural UI test for it. The flag is reachable by MCP, script params and the file.
- 2D Adaptive, Slot and the 3D roughing kinds (refused by name at the door for now).
- Holes in the model, typed points with an explicit "the hole exists" choice, carried stock from a previous setup, and a "pre-drilled only" refusal mode.
- Non-centre-cutting tools down a hole: the plunge law would need the proved holes.
- A user-set clearance (fixed at 0.1 mm a side).
- Golden CL file: the pins assert the moves and the posted lines directly.
- No hand check in the GUI or on a machine.

Changelog: 2D Pocket: pre-drilled entry - with `links.approach.predrilled` on, each level is entered by a straight plunge down a hole a Drill operation ahead of it in the setup made, only where the stock simulation proves the hole open wide and deep enough; elsewhere the asked entry stands, named (#1449, first slice)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Refs #1449

title: feat(ui): Setup page follows the WCS page's layout
body:
## What changed

Slice 5 (last) of #1440: the setup's own page (`SetupPage::Settings`, the "Setup1" node's properties page) follows the WCS page's layout. This is NOT the "Setups" list page (`pages.rs::setups_page`), a different page that stays as it is.

- Titled `layout::group` sections: Active setup, Stock source, Part orientation (with a one-line helper), Work offset, Workholding (only for a turning setup or one that states a limit), This setup (Delete / Open fixtures as two equal-width `even_row` buttons), then the stock entity / datum line as a small readout at the foot.
- With no setups the page is the one "First setup" group (message, pointer line, "Create first setup" button).
- New `setup_settings_page.rs` (the page body left `setup_pages.rs`). The pickers keep their controls and captions; the groups frame them. `setup_stock_pick` lost its bare "Stock" caption (the group title says it); `setup_workholding_row::shown` is the row's own test; `wcs_page::cell_w` is `pub(super)`.
- Page-wide indent 12 and item gap 4: the pick rows are as wide as the narrow pane (#330) and the default indent pushed "Point 1 to plane level" and the workholding Apply past its edge (the existing structural tests caught both).
- Layout only: no command, parameter or project-file change; every edit goes through its existing undoable command. No snapshot PNG touched.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1440-setup-page-tidy.md`.

## Series

The five pages of #1440: Stock #1460, Tool list #1465, Fixtures #1471, Machine #1472, Setup (this PR). `Refs #1440` only; the issue closes when all five merge.

## Overlap (stacking decision)

#773 (orientation dropdowns) changes five lines inside the old `settings()` (replaces the alignment, plane, points and axis calls with one `setup_orient_pick::section`). Not stacked: it is a contributor's draft on another fork (cannot push to it) and this PR moves those lines into the new file, so one small hunk resolves at whichever merges second (the call list goes into the "Part orientation" group). Expected textual overlaps: `setup_pages.rs` (#773, #1465, #1472; this PR deletes `settings()` and removes the `UiTarget` import), `wcs_page.rs` (`cell_w` `pub(super)`, the same one-line change as #1472, identical so it merges clean), `mod.rs` / `tests.rs` (module lists, adjacent additions), `setup_stock_pick.rs` and `setup_workholding_row.rs` (small). #1209 and #1124 touch `pages.rs` and the WCS flow, not this page.

## Pins (crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_settings_page.rs)

- the_setup_page_is_laid_out_in_groups_like_the_wcs_page: every group title in order; every label/button of every picker inside its own group in order; two equal action buttons on one row; foot readout.
- the_first_setups_page_has_no_previous_setup_rows (fresh/first setup: stock note, no relative / "leaves behind" rows).
- an_inactive_setups_page_draws_its_groups_and_the_radio_activates_it (inactive setup; radio click and undo).
- the_page_with_no_setups_offers_only_the_first_setup (empty document; button and undo).
- a_lathe_setup_draws_the_workholding_group (conditional group; Apply rpm then Clear rpm / Stated).
- the_armed_pick_rows_stay_inside_their_groups (plane, points and WCS armed rows: every conditionally drawn control).
- the_setup_actions_still_queue_their_commands, open_fixtures_activates_the_setup_and_opens_its_fixtures_page.

Mutation check (each mutation applied alone to `setup_settings_page.rs`, the 8 tests run): all 19 went red: dropped active radio, stock group, helper line, alignment / relative / plane / points / axes / work offset / WCS-features calls, workholding group (absent and always drawn), Delete command, Open fixtures focus, foot readout, Create first setup command, no-setups message, pointer line, a reordered Work offset group. Stays green / unpinned: the Primary, Apply axes and Clear axes rows (drawn only after an axis pick in the viewport, which needs a real face pick) and the group-title text of a collapsed group.

## Not exercised / known

- Pane still scrolls sideways on the long axes caption (unchanged, pre-existing).
- Space-padded pick captions ("    Part alignment") untouched: nine files that #773 / #746 also edit, and their tests match the padded strings.

## Gates

fork synced at v0.19-line main (branched from upstream/main 7c21c9c2). `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ok (63 s); camcraft-ui lib single-threaded from `crates/ui`: 682 passed; clippy `-p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

title: ci: post-merge batch gate on the self-hosted Linux runner
body:
Stacked on #1418 (merge it first). Its diff here includes #1418's commits until it merges; #1418 currently conflicts with main (not fixed here).

## What changed
- `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`: push to `main` + `workflow_dispatch` (input `ref`); `[self-hosted, linux]`; concurrency `post-merge-main`, cancel-in-progress; `cargo xtask gate batch` under `xvfb-run -a`; gate-logs + gate-output always uploaded; no token on disk during tests.
- Sharing with the cut: skips itself (green, notice) when a `cut.yml` run is queued/in progress or a same-repo `release/v*` PR is open (`.github/scripts/post-merge-skip.sh`). Chosen as the simplest rule that cannot starve a cut; the cut's release gate covers main then.
- Reporting (`.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh`, report job only, `issues: write`): one rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)`; red opens it (P1, source:agent, effort:low, area:build) or comments on the open one; green comments the sha and closes it. P0 when a failing step name matches golden|gcode|g_code|post (heuristic on binary names; follow-up: a real "posted output" tag).
- AGENTS.md: "Fixes are tested in the background" (workflow first, local batch is the fallback), "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted" (push to main allowed for self-hosted only, quoting the user), cut-runner section note. PROCESS_VERSION 61 (upstream is 60; #1418 also bumps, settled at merge). Decision: `docs/decisions/1451-post-merge-gate.md`.

actionlint clean on post-merge.yml and cut.yml; YAML parses; `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run`; both scripts run locally against a fake `gh` (idle / cut running / release PR open; red new, red existing with P0 escalation, green close, green no issue).

## Not exercised
The workflow itself (needs the runner and a merge to main), real `gh` search for the issue title, the artifact download in the report job. xtask untouched.

title: feat(ui,app): an async file picker opens models and projects in the browser
body:
Part of #31, the app and UI on wasm. This slice adds an **async file picker**, so a model or a project can be opened in the browser build. Until now every picker there answered "cancelled".

Fork synced at v0.18.0. The branch merges `upstream/main` (53a52f88) so that it diffs clean against `main`.

## What changed
- **`crates/ui/src/file_pick.rs`** (new): the browser picker. On wasm32, `open()` makes an `<input type=file>` whose `accept` comes from the dialog's filters, clicks it and returns at once. When the user has chosen, the file's name and bytes go into a thread-local inbox, and the next frame is woken through the egui context, which `shell_web` registers.
  - Files over 256 MiB (`BROWSER_READ_LIMIT`) are refused by name before they are read. A failed allocation in wasm aborts the tab.
  - The input and its change closure are held in one slot until the next pick, not `forget`ed, so a cancelled picker does not leak.
  - The inbox, `accept_attr` and `too_big` are plain Rust on every target.
- **`crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs`** (new):
  - `open_model_dialog` / `open_project_dialog`: rfd's synchronous dialog on native (unchanged), the async picker on wasm32.
  - Each frame, `drain_actions` turns every inbox entry into a `CommandKind::OpenPicked`. A model goes through `ImportModel::from_bytes` and `finish_import`: one undo step, and a same-named model is an update. A project goes through `project::open_noted`.
  - A failed read, a refused import, or a project that is not text or not JSON is said on the status line ("import refused: …" / "open failed: …") and changes nothing.
- **`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`**: `ImportModel::from_bytes(file_name, data, budget)`. It shares the path import's laws through `checked_budget`: IGES and unknown extensions refused, the STEP budget's bounds. It adds the `MAX_FILE_BYTES` cap and the finite-mesh gate. `geometry::import::parse_model_graded_within` is now `pub`.
- **`crates/ui/src/state.rs`**:
  - Two new `CommandKind` arms route to the functions above.
  - The model and project dialogs' filters are factored out (`mesh_dialog`, `project_dialog`) so both pickers ask with the same ones.
  - `open_project_path`'s reset is factored out as `reset_for_open`, so the bytes open retires the old document the same way. Behaviour is unchanged.
- No dependency added. The picker uses `eframe::web_sys` features that eframe already enables (`HtmlInputElement`, `File`, `FileList`, `Blob`).
- **Safari fix (after the user's hand check, 2026-11-13).** `State::run_click_actions` runs the queue at the end of the clicked frame when it holds an action that may open a chooser (Open model, Open project, the unsaved-changes answer). eframe runs that frame inside its `pointerup` listener, so `input.click()` now happens inside the user's click; before, the queue ran at the start of the next frame, from requestAnimationFrame, where Safari ignores it without a word. The hidden input is now attached to the page with `display:none` and removed when replaced. A chooser asked for from the Cmd/Ctrl+O shortcut (a later frame) says on the status line to click File > Model / File > Open if no chooser appeared.
- The browser build no longer starts with "no theme folder found beside the exe" (`theme_dir::startup_status`).
- **Merge with #1431 (main):** main refused Open model / Open project in the browser until this picker landed; `browser_files::refusal` no longer refuses them, `NEEDS_PICKER` now names the pickers still owed, and the #1431 tests assert the two cells live.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-file-picker.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning tests:
  - `crates/app/tests/import_bytes.rs`:
    - `picked_bytes_import_like_the_same_file_from_disk`: the same name, mesh and fidelity as the disk import, for STL, OBJ and STEP.
    - `picked_bytes_are_refused_by_name_never_a_panic`: IGES, an unknown extension, no extension, empty or corrupt files of each format, and a budget given for a non-STEP file.
  - `crates/ui/src/file_pick_tests.rs`:
    - `a_picked_model_imports_through_the_undoable_command`
    - `a_picked_file_that_cannot_be_used_is_refused_by_name`
    - `a_picked_project_opens_in_place_of_the_document`
    - `the_browser_picker_accepts_the_dialogs_extensions`
    - `a_file_over_the_browser_read_limit_is_refused_before_it_is_read`
    - `a_chooser_asked_for_by_a_click_opens_inside_that_click` (Safari fix)
    - `a_chooser_outside_a_click_says_what_to_do_instead_of_failing_silently` (Safari fix)
  - `theme_dir::tests::the_browser_build_never_says_a_theme_folder_is_missing_beside_an_exe`
  - `browser_files::tests::every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `egui_app::tests::browser_files::{the_ribbon_keeps_open_live_in_the_browser, a_picker_the_browser_lacks_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored}` (merge with #1431)
- **Safari fix push (head 0dd7eebc, merges upstream/main f84059c9):** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (app suites 69 s, ui suites 67 s); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` built with no camcraft warnings (stock macOS bash now runs it) and `web/check-app-page.sh target/web` passed. A plain `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` is not possible here: flecs' C needs the script's wasi sysroot.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. The app suites (lib, import_bytes, large_models, model_fidelity, step_*, stock_export, bore_facet_sagitta) passed in 21 s. The ui suites (lib, boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, theme_files) passed in 19 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (native, macOS).
- **wasm check**: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` passed on macOS, using the official rustc 1.99.1 with the wasm32 std and Homebrew LLVM's clang for the wasi C.
  - It linked `camcraft-cli.wasm` and `camcraft_ui.wasm`, ran wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 and laid out `target/web`. The shim answers all nine WASI imports.
  - camcraft-ui raised no warnings.
  - `web/check-app-page.sh target/web` passed.
  - The script needed two local workarounds, which are not part of this PR: a GNU-`sed -i` shim, and a bash-3.2 empty-array fix for `"${PROFILE_ARGS[@]}"` under `set -u` (line 104). As shipped, the script does not run on stock macOS bash/sed. Worth a small follow-up.

## Not exercised - browser hand check needed
- **The picker was not run in a browser.** It needs a hand check: serve `target/web`, then use File > Open model on an STL, OBJ and STEP file and File > Open project on a `.camproj`. Also check that cancel does nothing and that a file over 256 MiB is refused on the status line.
- **Safari fix verified by hand by the user on 2026-11-14 (build 32c66876 = 0dd7eebc tree).** The user's hand check (2026-11-13) passed in Chrome and Brave; in Safari, File > Open model opened no chooser and said nothing. The input was clicked from the next egui frame (requestAnimationFrame), outside the click; Safari ignores it there. It is now clicked at the end of the clicked frame, which eframe runs inside its `pointerup` listener (see the PR comment for the sources). The Cmd/Ctrl+O shortcut is still handed over on a later frame: in Safari it may not open the chooser, and the status line then says to click File > Model / File > Open.
- Still owed on #31 (see the decisions file):
  - The other pickers: fixture import, machine, post, theme and tool library.
  - Dropped files.
  - Inline playback, a WebGPU run, the in-browser CI job, console diagnostics for the app crate, and the shell.rs split.

Changelog: The browser build opens models (STL, OBJ, STEP) and projects through an async file picker (#31).
Effort: high (no escalation)

title: feat(edm): Wire Contour skim passes - per-pass condition, offset and direction
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551). fork synced at v0.19.0.

Expected merges: retarget to `main` after #1139 merges. #1143 (Wire UI, also on #1139) touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs`; this PR changes one line there (the op destructure gains `..`), so a trivial conflict at most. #534 (verify) and #1109 (open profile) on #1123 are not touched.

## What changed

The Wire Contour gains skim passes: a rough pass, then N skims, each naming its own machine condition (and so its own offset, wire radius + that condition's gap), with an optional direction reversal per skim.

- `operation::WireContourOp.skims: Vec<WireSkim { condition, reverse }>`; file / MCP JSON `skims: [{ condition, reverse? }]`, absent when empty (rough-only files and goldens unchanged). Edits ride `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the existing MCP params door.
- Command door (`wire_op::condition_of`): every skim's condition resolved through #531's door, refused by name when it names none or the machine does not state it; then `motion::wire_edm::check_passes`: a pass nearer the profile than the finishing (last) pass ("would cut past the finished profile", rough included), a skim farther out than the pass before it ("would cut only air"), a skim condition with another wire diameter ("one threading cuts every pass with one wire").
- Generator: `motion::wire_edm::wire_passes` (new `skims.rs`) runs #532's single-pass generator per pass at its own offset, every law at that offset; each pass leads in from the threading point and back; a reversed skim walks clockwise. No skims is `wire_contour` exactly.
- Stamp digests each skim's condition numbers and direction (writes nothing for no skims - no stored stamp moves).
- Post stream (`posting_wire`): a mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition <skim id>` before each skim's first move (after each return to the threading point); a path that does not return once per pass is refused.
- `wire-iso.cps`: a condition that arrives with the wire threaded is the next skim's - `(SKIM n)`, the condition select and `comp_off` again at its first move; the wire stays threaded.
- **Wire laws (#534) and skims** (merge with main, 2026-11-13): `sim::verify::wire` now judges each move at its own pass's kerf. Before this, every move was judged at the rough's kerf, which read skim 1 as a false 0.0200 mm gouge at move 8 (0.165 - 0.145). `WireJob.skim_offsets`, new `passes.rs`: the path is split at each return to the threading point, the threading law takes the widest pass, and the slug law sweeps each pass at its own offset. Skims on an open run are refused at the door and in the law. The arithmetic is in the decision record.
- **Sodick wire post refuses skims** (second merge-time refresh, main after #1506): `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` writes its C condition word once, at threading, so a skim's mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition` would only have reassigned a variable and every skim would have been cut on the rough pass's condition. A condition change after the section's first cut is now refused by name: "Sodick: a condition change between passes (skims) is not supported by this post - post the skims through wire-iso or as separate operations". No C word is written per pass (no public Sodick source for a mid-program condition change, #617). `wire-iso.cps` is the only other shipped wire post and already selects per pass, so it is unchanged. Main's `sodick_wire_post.rs` literal gains `skims`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md`.

## How tested

- New golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` (rough C110 + skim S21 + reversed skim S31 on #533's synthetic fixture): three distinct offsets (X-20.165 / -20.145 / -20.135), three condition selects, one thread, one cut.
- `wire_post`: `a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects`, `no_skims_is_the_rough_program_and_json_unchanged`, `skims_edit_undo_and_round_trip`, `each_skim_refusal_is_named_at_the_door`; the existing `the_punch_contour_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate` passes with #533's golden unchanged (no golden moved).
- `camcraft-motion` unit: `skims_cut_their_own_offsets_and_none_is_the_single_pass`, `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`.
- `camcraft-sim` unit: `verify::wire::tests::each_pass_is_judged_at_its_own_kerf`, `passes_that_cannot_be_told_apart_are_unreadable`.
- `wire_contour` suite (all 7) green; `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/533-wire-iso-post` on head 0e96ca1c: motion, app (every suite - the new golden is shared input) and ui suites, 0 failed (12.4 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

- `sodick_wire_post::skims_are_refused_by_name_never_cut_on_the_rough_condition`: a rough C110 + skims C121, C131 through `post_script` is refused by name with no file, and through the engine neither skim C word is written. **Mutation check:** with the refusal block removed from `sodick-wire.cps` the test is RED (the skimmed program posted, `expect_err` panicked); restored, GREEN. Sodick goldens and `wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` unchanged.
- Second refresh, head 7d8a125a: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` post, sim, motion, app, ui suites 0 failed (31.8 min), the four pinning tests included; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-{geometry,cl,tools,post,sim,motion,app,ui} --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the fixture's conditions and codes are synthetic (three synthetic conditions S21, S31, W20 added to it).
- A punch drops after its rough unless held - tabs are #539; the program does not claim a hold.

title: feat(app): work offsets post as an index bounded by the setup's own post (#931 slice 2)
body:
## What changed (slice 2 of 3: app)

Stacked on #1101 (slice 1, now refreshed on main at 3460d7ba; its former parent #945 merged 2026-11-12). #1124 (slice 3) stacks on this. Fork synced at v0.19.0. Effort: high.

The app now hands the post the setup's 1-based work-offset index, not a word. The setup's own post sets the limit; core keeps only a sanity bound.

- **The stream carries the index.** `camcraft_post::post::Dump::wcs` is now a `u32`, where 1 is the first offset. `posting::wcs_context` returns `(index, origin)`. The post writes the word.
- **No fallback (triage point 2).** `setup::work_offset` no longer filters the stored pick. If a setup's post cannot express the stored offset, the offset is still never read as offset 1 or G54. That holds for the stream, the travel check, the label and the setup sheet.
- **Post-time gate.** New `setup_offsets::range_problems`, part of `verification_report`, so it applies to the single-file, per-mount and per-op posts. It checks each setup that has an operation against that setup's own post (`setup_mount::post_of`). An offset the post cannot express blocks the post, naming the setup and the post. Slice 1's engine refusal still runs behind it.
- **Command-time check.** `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` checks the pick against the setup's post (`setup_offsets::check`) and refuses by name.
- **Loader.** The six-offset cap is removed from `project/apply.rs`. Only the sanity bound remains (pick 0..=254, the `u8` that the height digest stores).
- **Names.** New `setup::work_offset_names(world, setup)` reads slice 1's `work_offsets(cps)` table. It is cached per (resolved post, script text) in a bounded map. `setup::offset_name`, `setup::wcs_name` and `setup::wcs_label` use it, and so do the setup sheet, the refusal texts, the spindle-law text and the shared-offset clause. The names are for display only and never go into the stream.
- **File format.** Offsets 1-6 are still saved as `G54`..`G59`, so existing files round-trip byte-identical. Offsets 7 and up are saved as their number. **Builds older than this one cannot open a file that uses offset 7 or higher.** The decision file records this for the release notes (point 8).
- **`WCS_SLOTS` is split (point 1).** It is now a crate-private `LEGACY_WCS_NAMES`, used only for legacy entity-name reservations and the pre-v52 and pre-v54 migrations. All of its word uses are gone.
- **`shared_word_problems` (point 7)** compares offset indexes and names the offset by the post's name.
- **UI and MCP** keep working through the app functions. The Setups combo still lists offsets 1-6, now named by the setup's post. MCP still accepts the words G54-G59. Slice 3 changes the combo and adds MCP's `index`.

## How tested

- Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/wcs_index.rs`:
  - `offset_nine_on_a_six_offset_post_refuses_by_setup_name_and_never_posts_at_offset_one` (the no-fallback pin)
  - `the_command_refuses_an_offset_the_setups_post_cannot_express`
  - `the_setups_post_names_its_offsets`
  - `offset_seven_and_up_saves_as_its_number_and_reloads`
- Unit test: `project::wcs_pick::tests::legacy_words_and_numbers_round_trip`.
- **Refresh 2871b646** (refreshed #1101 merged, bringing upstream/main 2d15a617): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green - post suites, app suites, ui suites: 3823 passed, 0 failed (37.2 min wall); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. No recorded stream, script or golden changed in the refresh.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 671ccd19: post suites, about 250 app suites including `wcs_index`, `setup_wcs`, `posting`, `probe_*`, `project_roundtrip` and `conformance`, the ui lib plus 11 ui suites. Wall time 9.6 min.
- I also ran 23 golden and post suites that the quick gate does not pick, including `golden_cl`, `carvera_post`, `heidenhain_*`, `tormach_post` and `lathe_post_*`. All pass, and no golden file changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- GUI hand check and Hub run: both done on #1124's head d97157c2, which contains this slice. **Hub run PASS** (2026-11-13, the user, PathPilot v2.14.4 770MX sim): G54, G59, G59.1, G59.2, G59.3 all cut, no unknown-word error; G54/G59 byte-identical to main's; offset 10 refused by name. The GUI hand check (macOS release build of d97157c2, 2026-11-12) passed.
- A user `.cps` file post with extended offsets was not tried by hand. It goes through the same cache path as the built-in posts.

#1101's Hub run is done (pass). Like #1101, it merges at the next cut, after #1101.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-app.md`.

Changelog: Work offsets are an index whose limit and names come from each setup's post. An offset the post cannot express is refused by setup name instead of posting at G54. Offsets 7 and up are saved as their number, and older builds cannot open those files. (#931)

title: feat(post): work offsets ride the stream as a 1-based index; the post writes the word
body:
Slice 1 of 3 for #931: the post crate and scripts. Based on main (#945, its former parent, merged 2026-11-12). #1113 (slice 2) stacks on this, and #1124 (slice 3) on #1113. Fork synced at v0.19.0. Effort: high.

**This changes the post interface** (what every script receives as `PARAM WorkOffset`), so it was held for a Hub run.

**Hub run: PASS** (2026-11-13, the user): posted from #1124's head d97157c2 (contains this slice) with the Tormach PathPilot post on the 770MX sim (PathPilot v2.14.4), five setups at G54, G59, G59.1, G59.2, G59.3: no unknown-word error, G59.1/G59.3 shown active, all five squares cut, M30. G54 and G59 output byte-identical to main's; offset 10 refused by name. The merge-time refresh at 3460d7ba leaves this PR's diff against main line-for-line identical to e188b4f6's, so the tested output stands.

## What changed

- **The stream carries the index.** `dump` writes `PARAM WorkOffset` as the setup's 1-based offset number (`G55` -> `2`). App still hands the word and still caps at 6; slice 2 makes the `Dump` field an index.
- **New `workOffsetIndex` manifest flag** (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs`, on the `coolantModes` pattern). It is read once at load with `workOffsetMax` (6 when unstated):
  - A flagged script receives the number. The engine refuses an offset above its maximum by setup name.
  - An unflagged (user) script receives the word `G54`..`G59` for 1-6, exactly as before. Any offset above 6 is refused by setup name, and an unflagged script cannot raise its own maximum.
  - The legacy words `G54`..`G59` in a stream still read as 1-6. Any other value (`G53`, 0, 2.5, `G54.1 P3`) is refused by setup name before a script sees it.
  - `work_offset::work_offsets(cps)` returns the maximum and the `workOffsetName(n)` names for slice 2's display. It never feeds the stream.
- **All 11 scripts shipped when this was written** declare the flag (grblhal.cps and tinyg.cps, added to main later, do not yet: they stay on the unflagged path, offsets 1-6, follow-up #1385), `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName`, and map the index to their own word. No `slotOf` / `frameWord` / `frameOf` word parsing remains:
  - The Fanuc-family probe register reads `wcsIndex - 1`.
  - Sinumerik's `$P_UIFR[n]` uses the number directly.
  - Heidenhain maps offset n to preset row n.
- **Declared maxima:**
  - Tormach mill and Tormach lathe: **9** (`G59.1`..`G59.3`, cited to the LinuxCNC G-code reference: "G54-G59.3 Select Coordinate System (1 - 9)" and its G10 L2 table).
  - Every other dialect: **6**. Haas G154, Fanuc/Mazak/Doosan G54.1 P and further Sinumerik/Heidenhain frames or rows were not verified against a public manual, so none is written. Reasons and sources are in `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-post.md`.
- **Docs.** `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents the 1-based `WorkOffset` beside the probe's 0-based `SetWorkOffset` (triage point 4). `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describes the flag, the maximum and the name function.

## Tests

- **Refresh 3460d7ba** (upstream/main 2d15a617 merged): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (post suites + 93 app suites, 1093 passed, 0 failed, incl. work_offset_index 9/9); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

- New `crates/post/tests/work_offset_index.rs` (9 tests). Every shipped script runs on recorded streams at offsets 1, 6, 7, its maximum and one past it, checking the word it writes or the refusal by setup name. It also covers:
  - a recorded generator toolpath (`face_square_40x40.cl`) through Fanuc and Tormach;
  - legacy word streams posting byte-identically to their index;
  - invalid values;
  - an unflagged user script at 1-6 and at 7, and one that tries to raise its maximum;
  - a flagged script without a maximum or names;
  - the dump writing the index;
  - each script's name table.
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_refuses_a_work_offset_that_names_no_settable_frame` now expects the engine's refusal of `G53` (the engine refuses it before the script runs).
- Gate (local, worktree target, sccache), on head `2fe7afb7`:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
  - 63 app suites, 431 passed, 0 failed. They cover every app suite that posts through the shipped scripts: conformance, golden_cl, posting, arc_planes, cli, the probe_* suites, sinumerik_*, heidenhain_*, fanuc_post, doosan_dnm_post, carvera_*, tormach_*, the lathe_post* suites, plasma_*, inverted_*, comment_escape, one_wcs, setups, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, rotated_wcs, setup_mounts_post, setup_post_options, per_op_files, program_comments, smoothing, after_op, coolant*, post_unit_word, regression_models, wear_comp, control_comp and lathe_spindle_law. There are no separate mazak or haas suites; those scripts are covered by conformance, fanuc_post and the inverted_* suites.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- 400-line law: the new manifest reading lives in its own module, `work_offset.rs`. `engine.rs` (511 -> 530 lines) and `js.rs` (409 -> 415) were already over 400 and grew only by the hook-up.

**Goldens:** no golden file changed. Offsets 1-6 post the same words as before.

**Not exercised:** the GUI and MCP (unchanged in this slice), a real control, and offsets above 6 end to end through app (app still caps at 6 until slice 2).

Changelog: Posts receive the work offset as a 1-based number and write their own word; the Tormach mill and lathe posts accept work offsets 7-9 (G59.1-G59.3), and a post that cannot express an offset refuses it by setup name (#931, slice 1)

title: fix(ui,app): setup alignment composes on the current pose, one flow, readable picks (#738)
body:
## What changed (#738, maintainer-reported, P1)

1. **Moves compose on the current pose.** Laying on a face or on three points now computes the lay in the setup's current alignment and composes it onto that alignment, through new `pick::lay_on_plane_in` / `lay_on_points_in` and `setup_turn::held_centre`. Before, each move went back to the import pose first. Axes already composed. Each move is still one `AlignPartToSetup`, and one undo returns to the previous pose exactly. Re-applying the same pick is a zero step and is refused as "already holds the part that way".
